verses.1:1: Seeing that many have undertaken to arrange an account concerning the things that have been fully accomplished among us,
verses.1:2: just as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and servants of the word handed them down to us,
verses.1:3: it seemed fitting to me also, having closely followed all things from the very first, to write to you in orderly sequence, most noble Theophilus,
verses.1:4: that you may fully know the certainty concerning the words in which you were instructed.
verses.1:5: In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a certain priest by the name of Zechariah, of the priestly division of Abijah. He had a wife from the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
verses.1:6: And both of them were righteous in the sight of God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and statutes of the Lord.
verses.1:7: Yet they had no child, because Elizabeth was barren, and both of them were well advanced in their days.
verses.1:8: Now it came to pass, while he was serving in the priestly office before God in the order of his division,
verses.1:9: that according to the custom of the priesthood, it fell to him by lot to burn incense upon entering the sanctuary of the Lord.
verses.1:10: And the entire multitude of the people was outside praying at the hour of the incense offering.
verses.1:11: And there appeared to him an angel of the Lord, standing on the right of the altar of incense.
verses.1:12: And when Zechariah beheld him, he was troubled, and fear fell upon him.
verses.1:13: But the angel said to him, "Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your supplication has been heard; and your wife Elizabeth shall bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.
verses.1:14: And joy and exultation shall be yours, and many shall rejoice at his birth.
verses.1:15: For he shall be great before the Lord, and he shall never drink wine or strong drink; and he shall be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb.
verses.1:16: And he shall turn many of the sons of Israel back to the Lord their God.
verses.1:17: And he himself shall go forth before Him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers toward their children, and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous, to make ready for the Lord a prepared people."
verses.1:18: And Zechariah said to the angel, "By what means shall I know this? For I am an aged man, and my wife is well advanced in her days."
verses.1:19: And answering, the angel said to him, "I am Gabriel, who stands before God; and I was sent to speak with you and to declare to you these good tidings.
verses.1:20: And behold, you shall be silent and unable to speak until the day these things come to pass, because you did not believe my words, which shall be fulfilled in their appointed season."
verses.1:21: And the people were waiting expectantly for Zechariah, and they marveled that he lingered so long in the sanctuary.
verses.1:22: Yet when he came out, he could not speak to them, and they recognized that he had seen a vision in the sanctuary; and he kept making signs to them and remained speechless.
verses.1:23: And it came to pass, when the days of his ministry were fulfilled, that he departed to his own house.
verses.1:24: Now after those days his wife Elizabeth conceived, and she kept herself in seclusion for five months, saying,
verses.1:25: "Thus the Lord has done for me in the days in which He looked upon me, to take away my reproach among men."
verses.1:26: And in the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent forth from God to a city of Galilee whose name was Nazareth,
verses.1:27: to a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, from the house of David; and the name of the virgin was Mary.
verses.1:28: And the angel came in to her and said, "Rejoice, O favored one! The Lord is with you."
verses.1:29: But she was greatly troubled at this saying, and pondered what manner of greeting this might be.
verses.1:30: And the angel said to her, "Do not fear, Mary, for you have found favor before God.
verses.1:31: And behold, you shall conceive in your womb and give birth to a Son, and you shall call His name Jesus.
verses.1:32: He shall be great and shall be called the Son of the Most High; and the Lord God shall give to Him the throne of His father David,
verses.1:33: and He shall reign over the house of Jacob forevermore, and to His kingdom there shall be no end."
verses.1:34: But Mary said to the angel, "How shall this come to pass, since I do not know a man?"
verses.1:35: And answering, the angel said to her, "The Holy Spirit shall come upon you, and the power of the Most High shall overshadow you; therefore also the Child to be born shall be called holy, the Son of God.
verses.1:36: And behold, Elizabeth your kinswoman has herself also conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month with her who was called barren;
verses.1:37: for no word from God shall be impossible."
verses.1:38: And Mary said, "Behold, the handmaid of the Lord; may it be to me according to your word." And the angel departed from her.
verses.1:39: In those days Mary arose and journeyed with haste into the hill country, to a city of Judah,
verses.1:40: and she entered into the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.
verses.1:41: And it came to pass, as soon as Elizabeth heard Mary's greeting, that the babe leaped within her womb; and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
verses.1:42: And she exclaimed with a loud voice and said, "Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
verses.1:43: And how has this come about for me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
verses.1:44: For behold, the moment the voice of your greeting came to my ears, the babe leaped within my womb in exultation.
verses.1:45: And blessed is she who believed that there shall be a fulfillment of the things spoken to her from the Lord."
verses.1:46: And Mary said, "My soul magnifies the Lord,
verses.1:47: and my spirit has exulted in God my Savior;
verses.1:48: for He has looked upon the lowliness of His handmaid; for behold, from this time onward all generations shall call me blessed.
verses.1:49: For the Mighty One has done great things for me, and His name is holy;
verses.1:50: and His mercy extends to generations and generations upon those who fear Him.
verses.1:51: He has shown might with His arm; He has scattered the proud in the intent of their heart.
verses.1:52: He has cast down rulers from thrones and exalted the humble;
verses.1:53: the hungry He has filled with good things, and the rich He has sent away empty.
verses.1:54: He has come to the aid of Israel His servant, to remember mercy,
verses.1:55: just as He spoke to our forefathers, to Abraham and to his seed forevermore."
verses.1:56: Now Mary remained with her for about three months, and then returned to her own house.
verses.1:57: Now Elizabeth's time to give birth was fulfilled, and she brought forth a son.
verses.1:58: And her neighbors and kinsfolk heard that the Lord had magnified His mercy toward her, and they rejoiced together with her.
verses.1:59: And it came to pass, on the eighth day, that they came to circumcise the child; and they were about to name him Zechariah, after the name of his father.
verses.1:60: And his mother answered and said, "By no means; rather, he shall be called John."
verses.1:61: And they said to her, "Not one of your kindred is called by this name."
verses.1:62: Then they made signs to his father as to what he wished him to be named.
verses.1:63: And he asked for a writing tablet and wrote, saying, "John is his name." And all of them marveled.
verses.1:64: And at once his mouth was opened and his tongue was freed, and he began to speak, blessing God.
verses.1:65: And fear came upon all those dwelling around them; and throughout the entire hill country of Judea all these things were talked about,
verses.1:66: and all who heard laid them up in their hearts, saying, "What then shall this child be?" For indeed the hand of the Lord was with him.
verses.1:67: Then Zechariah his father was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying,
verses.1:68: "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for He has visited and brought redemption to His people,
verses.1:69: and has raised up for us a horn of salvation in the house of David His servant,
verses.1:70: just as He spoke by the mouth of His holy prophets from ages past,
verses.1:71: salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us,
verses.1:72: to show mercy toward our forefathers and to remember His holy covenant,
verses.1:73: the oath which He swore to Abraham our father, to grant to us
verses.1:74: that, delivered from the hand of enemies, we might serve Him without fear
verses.1:75: in holiness and righteousness in His presence all our days.
verses.1:76: And you also, little child, shall be called prophet of the Most High; for you shall go forth before the Lord to make ready His ways,
verses.1:77: to give the knowledge of salvation to His people in the remission of their sins,
verses.1:78: because of the tender mercy of our God, by which the Dawn from on high shall visit us,
verses.1:79: to shine upon those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, to direct our feet into the way of peace."
verses.1:80: And the child grew and became strong in spirit, and he was in the desert places until the day of his public appearing to Israel.
verses.2:1: Now it came to pass in those days that a decree went forth from Caesar Augustus for all the inhabited world to be enrolled.
verses.2:2: (This first enrollment took place while Quirinius was governor of Syria.)
verses.2:3: And all were going to be enrolled, each one to his own city.
verses.2:4: And Joseph also ascended from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to the city of David, which is named Bethlehem, because he belonged to the house and lineage of David,
verses.2:5: to be enrolled with Mary, who was betrothed to him, being with child.
verses.2:6: Now it came to pass, while they were there, that the days were fulfilled for her to give birth.
verses.2:7: And she gave birth to her firstborn Son, and wrapped Him in swaddling bands, and laid Him down in a manger, because there was no room for them in the lodging place.
verses.2:8: Now in that same region there were shepherds abiding in the open fields, keeping the watches of the night over their flock.
verses.2:9: And an angel of the Lord stood beside them, and the glory of the Lord shone all around them, and they feared with a great fear.
verses.2:10: And the angel said to them, "Do not fear, for behold, I proclaim to you glad tidings of great joy, which shall be for all the people,
verses.2:11: for to you is born this day a Savior, who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David;
verses.2:12: and this shall be the sign for you: you shall find an infant wrapped in swaddling bands and lying in a manger."
verses.2:13: And suddenly there came to be with the angel a multitude of the host of heaven, praising God and saying,
verses.2:14: "Glory to God in the highest, and upon earth peace among men of His good pleasure."
verses.2:15: And it happened, when the angels had departed from them into heaven, that the shepherds were saying to one another, "Let us go across now to Bethlehem and behold this matter that has taken place, which the Lord has made known to us."
verses.2:16: And they came in haste and found both Mary and Joseph, and the infant lying in the manger.
verses.2:17: And having seen, they made known concerning the word that had been spoken to them about this Child.
verses.2:18: And all who heard marveled concerning the things spoken to them by the shepherds,
verses.2:19: but Mary treasured all these words, pondering them in her heart.
verses.2:20: And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all that they had heard and seen, just as it had been spoken to them.
verses.2:21: And when eight days were fulfilled to circumcise Him, His name was called Jesus, as He had been named by the angel before He was conceived in the womb.
verses.2:22: And when the days of their purification were fulfilled according to the Law of Moses, they brought Him up to Jerusalem to present Him to the Lord,
verses.2:23: just as it is written in the law of the Lord, "Every male that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord,"
verses.2:24: and to offer a sacrifice according to what has been spoken in the law of the Lord: a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.
verses.2:25: And behold, in Jerusalem there was a man whose name was Simeon, and this man was righteous and reverent, looking for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him.
verses.2:26: And it had been divinely revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he should see the Christ of the Lord.
verses.2:27: And he entered the temple in the Spirit; and as the parents brought in the Child Jesus, that they might do concerning Him according to the custom of the law,
verses.2:28: he himself took Him into his arms, blessed God, and said,
verses.2:29: "Now You dismiss Your servant, O Sovereign Lord, according to Your word, in peace;
verses.2:30: for my eyes have beheld Your salvation,
verses.2:31: which You have made ready in the presence of all the peoples:
verses.2:32: a light for revelation to the Gentiles, and glory for Your people Israel."
verses.2:33: And His father and His mother were marveling at the things being spoken concerning Him.
verses.2:34: And Simeon blessed them and said to Mary His mother, "Behold, this Child is set for the fall and rising up of many in Israel, and for a sign that is spoken against—
verses.2:35: and a sword shall pierce through your own soul also—so that the thoughts out of many hearts may be revealed."
verses.2:36: And there was Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher (she was well advanced in years, having lived with a husband seven years from her virginity,
verses.2:37: and she had been a widow up to eighty-four years of age), who did not depart from the temple, worshiping with fastings and supplications night and day.
verses.2:38: And coming up at that very hour, she gave thanks to God and spoke concerning Him to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.
verses.2:39: And when they had completed everything according to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city of Nazareth.
verses.2:40: And the Child grew and increased in strength, being filled with wisdom; and the grace of God was upon Him.
verses.2:41: Now His parents traveled every year to Jerusalem at the Feast of the Passover.
verses.2:42: And when He became twelve years old, as they went up according to the custom of the feast
verses.2:43: and had completed the days, as they were returning, the boy Jesus remained behind in Jerusalem, and His parents did not know it.
verses.2:44: But supposing Him to be in the company of travelers, they went a day's journey and were searching for Him among their kinsfolk and acquaintances.
verses.2:45: And when they did not find Him, they turned back to Jerusalem, searching for Him.
verses.2:46: And it came to pass after three days that they found Him in the temple, seated in the midst of the teachers, hearing them and questioning them;
verses.2:47: and all who were listening to Him were astounded at His discernment and His replies.
verses.2:48: And when they saw Him, they were astonished; and His mother said to Him, "Child, why have You treated us like this? Behold, Your father and I have been searching for You in distress."
verses.2:49: And He said to them, "Why is it that you were seeking Me? Did you not know that I must be in the house of My Father?"
verses.2:50: Yet they did not comprehend the saying that He spoke to them.
verses.2:51: And He went down with them and came to Nazareth, and He continued in subjection to them. And His mother treasured up all the sayings in her heart.
verses.2:52: And Jesus advanced in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and with men.
verses.3:1: Now in the fifteenth year of the rule of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governing Judea, and Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, and his brother Philip was tetrarch of the region of Iturea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene,
verses.3:2: during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came upon John the son of Zechariah in the wilderness.
verses.3:3: And he went into all the surrounding region of the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins,
verses.3:4: as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: "A voice of one crying out in the wilderness: 'Prepare the way of the Lord; make straight His paths.'
verses.3:5: Every valley shall be filled up, and every mountain and hill shall be made low; and the crooked places shall become straight, and the rough places smooth ways;
verses.3:6: and all flesh shall see the salvation of God."
verses.3:7: Therefore he said to the crowds coming out to be baptized by him, "Offspring of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
verses.3:8: Bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say within yourselves, 'We have Abraham as our father'; for I say to you that out of these stones God is able to raise up children for Abraham.
verses.3:9: And already the ax also lies at the root of the trees; therefore every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and cast into the fire."
verses.3:10: And the crowds were questioning him, saying, "What then shall we do?"
verses.3:11: And answering, he said to them, "Let the one who has two tunics share with the one who has none, and let the one who has food do likewise."
verses.3:12: And tax collectors also came to be baptized, and they said to him, "Teacher, what shall we do?"
verses.3:13: And he said to them, "Exact nothing more than what has been prescribed for you."
verses.3:14: And soldiers also questioned him, saying, "And what shall we ourselves do?" And he said to them, "Do not extort from anyone by intimidation, nor accuse anyone falsely, and be content with your wages."
verses.3:15: Now while the people were waiting in expectation, and all were pondering in their hearts concerning John, whether perhaps he himself might be the Christ,
verses.3:16: John answered, saying to them all, "As for me, I baptize you with water; yet the One who is mightier than I is coming, the strap of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie. He Himself will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
verses.3:17: His winnowing fork is in His hand to cleanse His threshing floor thoroughly and to gather the wheat into His granary, but the chaff He will burn up with unquenchable fire."
verses.3:18: Thus, with many other exhortations as well, he proclaimed the good news to the people.
verses.3:19: But Herod the tetrarch, when he was reproved by him concerning Herodias his brother's wife, and concerning all the wicked things that Herod had done,
verses.3:20: added this also above all the rest: he shut John up in prison.
verses.3:21: Now it came to pass, when all the people were baptized, and as Jesus too had been baptized and was praying, that heaven was opened,
verses.3:22: and the Holy Spirit descended upon Him in bodily appearance like a dove, and a voice came out of heaven: "You are My beloved Son; with You I am well pleased."
verses.3:23: And Jesus Himself, as He began His ministry, was about thirty years of age, being the son, as was supposed, of Joseph, the son of Heli,
verses.3:24: the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,
verses.3:25: the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Esli, the son of Naggai,
verses.3:26: the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Josech, the son of Joda,
verses.3:27: the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri,
verses.3:28: the son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmadam, the son of Er,
verses.3:29: the son of Joshua, the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi,
verses.3:30: the son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonam, the son of Eliakim,
verses.3:31: the son of Melea, the son of Menna, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David,
verses.3:32: the son of Jesse, the son of Jobel, the son of Boaz, the son of Sala, the son of Nahshon,
verses.3:33: the son of Amminadab, the son of Admin, the son of Arni, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah,
verses.3:34: the son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor,
verses.3:35: the son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah,
verses.3:36: the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech,
verses.3:37: the son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalalel, the son of Cainan,
verses.3:38: the son of Enosh, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.
verses.4:1: Now Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit in the wilderness
verses.4:2: for forty days, being tempted by the devil. And He ate nothing during those days, and when they had come to an end, He became hungry.
verses.4:3: Then the devil said to Him, "If You are the Son of God, speak to this stone that it may become bread."
verses.4:4: And Jesus replied to him, "It is written, 'Man shall not live on bread alone.'"
verses.4:5: And leading Him up, he showed Him all the kingdoms of the inhabited world in an instant of time.
verses.4:6: And the devil said to Him, "To You I will give all this authority and their glory, for it has been delivered to me, and to whomever I desire I give it.
verses.4:7: If You, therefore, worship before me, it shall all be Yours."
verses.4:8: And Jesus answered and said to him, "It is written, 'The Lord your God you shall worship, and Him alone you shall serve.'"
verses.4:9: Then he led Him to Jerusalem and set Him upon the pinnacle of the temple, and said to Him, "If You are the Son of God, cast Yourself down from here;
verses.4:10: for it is written, 'He shall command His angels concerning You, to guard You carefully,'
verses.4:11: and, 'On their hands they shall lift You up, lest You strike Your foot against a stone.'"
verses.4:12: And answering, Jesus said to him, "It has been said, 'You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.'"
verses.4:13: And when the devil had finished every temptation, he withdrew from Him until an opportune season.
verses.4:14: And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee, and a report concerning Him went forth through all the surrounding region.
verses.4:15: And He Himself was teaching in their synagogues, being glorified by all.
verses.4:16: And He came to Nazareth, where He had been raised; and according to His custom, He entered into the synagogue on the Sabbath day and stood up to read.
verses.4:17: And the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to Him; and unrolling the scroll, He found the place where it was written:
verses.4:18: "The Spirit of the Lord is upon Me, because He has anointed Me to bring good tidings to the poor; He has sent Me to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to send forth the oppressed in liberty,
verses.4:19: to herald the acceptable year of the Lord."
verses.4:20: And rolling up the scroll, He returned it to the attendant and sat down. And the eyes of all in the synagogue were fixed intently upon Him.
verses.4:21: Then He began to speak to them, "Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing."
verses.4:22: And all bore witness to Him and marveled at the words of grace that proceeded from His mouth, and they said, "Is this not the son of Joseph?"
verses.4:23: And He said to them, "No doubt you will say this proverb to Me: 'Physician, heal yourself! Whatever we heard took place in Capernaum, do here also in Your own homeland.'"
verses.4:24: And He said, "Assuredly, I say to you, no prophet is acceptable in his own homeland.
verses.4:25: And in truth I tell you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when heaven was shut up for three years and six months, when a great famine came upon all the land;
verses.4:26: yet Elijah was sent to none of them, but only to Zarephath in the territory of Sidon, to a woman who was a widow.
verses.4:27: And many lepers were in Israel during the time of Elisha the prophet, yet not one of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian."
verses.4:28: And all in the synagogue were filled with wrath as they heard these things,
verses.4:29: and rising up, they drove Him out of the city and led Him to the brow of the hill on which their city had been built, in order to hurl Him down the cliff.
verses.4:30: But He, passing through the midst of them, went on His way.
verses.4:31: And He went down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee; and He was teaching them on the Sabbath days.
verses.4:32: And they were astounded at His teaching, because His word was with authority.
verses.4:33: And in the synagogue there was a man having a spirit of an unclean demon, and he cried out with a loud voice,
verses.4:34: "Ah! What have we to do with You, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know You, who You are—the Holy One of God!"
verses.4:35: And Jesus rebuked it, saying, "Be silent, and come out of him!" And throwing him down in their midst, the demon came out of him, doing him no harm.
verses.4:36: And amazement came upon all, and they spoke together with one another, saying, "What is this word, that with authority and power He commands the unclean spirits, and they come out?"
verses.4:37: And news concerning Him went forth into every place of the surrounding region.
verses.4:38: Now arising from the synagogue, He entered into the house of Simon. And Simon's mother-in-law was afflicted with a high fever, and they appealed to Him on her behalf.
verses.4:39: And standing over her, He rebuked the fever, and it left her; and immediately she arose and ministered to them.
verses.4:40: Now as the sun was setting, all who had any suffering from various diseases brought them to Him; and laying His hands upon each one of them, He healed them.
verses.4:41: And demons also were coming out of many, crying out and saying, "You are the Son of God!" Yet rebuking them, He did not permit them to speak, because they knew Him to be the Christ.
verses.4:42: Now when day came, He departed and went to a desolate place; and the multitudes searched for Him and came to Him, and tried to detain Him so that He would not depart from them.
verses.4:43: But He said to them, "I must bring the good tidings of the kingdom of God to the other cities also, because for this purpose I was sent."
verses.4:44: And He continued preaching in the synagogues of Judea.
verses.5:1: Now it came to pass, while the multitude pressed upon Him and heard the word of God, that He was standing beside the Lake of Gennesaret,
verses.5:2: and He saw two boats standing by the lake; but the fishermen had stepped out of them and were washing their nets.
verses.5:3: Then He stepped into one of the boats, which was Simon's, and asked him to put out a little from the land. And sitting down, He taught the multitudes from the boat.
verses.5:4: When He had ceased speaking, He said to Simon, "Put out into the deep water, and let down your nets for a catch."
verses.5:5: And Simon answered and said, "Master, we have labored through the whole night and caught nothing; yet at Your word I will let down the nets."
verses.5:6: And when they had done this, they enclosed a great multitude of fish, and their nets were beginning to tear.
verses.5:7: So they signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them. And they came and filled both boats, so that they began to sink.
verses.5:8: When Simon Peter saw this, he fell down at the knees of Jesus, saying, "Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord!"
verses.5:9: For astonishment had seized him and all those with him at the catch of fish which they had taken,
verses.5:10: and likewise also James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon. And Jesus said to Simon, "Do not be afraid; from now on you shall be catching men alive."
verses.5:11: And when they had brought the boats to land, they forsook all and followed Him.
verses.5:12: And it came to pass, while He was in one of the cities, that behold, a man full of leprosy was there. Seeing Jesus, he fell upon his face and implored Him, saying, "Lord, if You are willing, You are able to cleanse me."
verses.5:13: Then He stretched out His hand and touched him, saying, "I am willing; be cleansed." And immediately the leprosy departed from him.
verses.5:14: And He charged him to tell no one, "but go and show yourself to the priest, and make an offering for your cleansing, just as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."
verses.5:15: Yet the report concerning Him spread all the more, and great multitudes gathered together to hear and to be healed of their infirmities.
verses.5:16: But He Himself would withdraw into the desolate places and pray.
verses.5:17: Now it came to pass on one of those days, while He was teaching, that Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there, who had come from every village of Galilee and Judea and from Jerusalem. And the power of the Lord was present for Him to heal.
verses.5:18: And behold, men were carrying on a bed a man who was paralyzed, and they sought to bring him in and set him down before Him.
verses.5:19: And not finding any way to bring him in because of the multitude, they went up onto the housetop and let him down through the tiles with his couch into the midst before Jesus.
verses.5:20: And seeing their faith, He said, "Man, your sins have been forgiven you."
verses.5:21: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, "Who is this who speaks blasphemies? Who is able to forgive sins except God alone?"
verses.5:22: But Jesus, perceiving their reasonings, answered and said to them, "Why do you reason in your hearts?
verses.5:23: Which is easier, to say, 'Your sins have been forgiven you,' or to say, 'Arise and walk'?
verses.5:24: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins"—He said to the paralyzed man, "I say to you, arise, take up your couch, and go to your house."
verses.5:25: And at once he rose up before them, took up that on which he had been lying, and departed to his house, glorifying God.
verses.5:26: And amazement seized them all, and they glorified God and were filled with fear, saying, "We have seen extraordinary things today!"
verses.5:27: And after these things He went forth and beheld a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax office. And He said to him, "Follow Me."
verses.5:28: And leaving all behind, he rose up and followed Him.
verses.5:29: Then Levi held a great banquet for Him in his house; and there was a great multitude of tax collectors and others who were reclining at table with them.
verses.5:30: And the Pharisees and their scribes murmured against His disciples, saying, "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
verses.5:31: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Those who are healthy have no need of a physician, but those who are sick.
verses.5:32: I have come not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance."
verses.5:33: Then they said to Him, "The disciples of John fast often and offer supplications, and likewise those of the Pharisees, but Yours eat and drink."
verses.5:34: And Jesus said to them, "Can you make the sons of the bridal chamber fast while the bridegroom is with them?
verses.5:35: Yet the days will come, and when the bridegroom is taken away from them, then they shall fast in those days."
verses.5:36: Then He also spoke a parable to them: "No one tears a patch from a new garment and puts it on an old garment; otherwise he will both tear the new, and the patch from the new will not match the old.
verses.5:37: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the new wine will burst the wineskins, and it will be spilled, and the wineskins will be ruined.
verses.5:38: Rather, new wine must be put into fresh wineskins.
verses.5:39: And no one, having drunk old wine, desires new; for he says, 'The old is good.'"
verses.6:1: Now it came to pass on a Sabbath that He was passing through the grainfields, and His disciples were plucking the heads of grain and eating them, rubbing them with their hands.
verses.6:2: And certain of the Pharisees said, "Why are you doing that which is not lawful on the Sabbath?"
verses.6:3: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Have you not even read this, what David did when he was hungry, he and those who were with him,
verses.6:4: how he entered into the house of God, and taking the bread of the Presence, ate it and gave it to those with him, which it is not lawful for any to eat except the priests alone?"
verses.6:5: And He told them, "The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath."
verses.6:6: Now it came to pass on another Sabbath that He entered the synagogue and taught; and there was a man there, and his right hand was withered.
verses.6:7: And the scribes and the Pharisees watched Him closely, whether He would heal on the Sabbath, that they might find grounds to accuse Him.
verses.6:8: But He knew their thoughts, and said to the man who had the withered hand, "Arise and stand in the midst." And rising up, he stood there.
verses.6:9: Then Jesus said to them, "I ask you, is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?"
verses.6:10: And having looked around at them all, He said to him, "Stretch out your hand." And he did so, and his hand was restored.
verses.6:11: But they were filled with fury, and conferred with one another concerning what they might do to Jesus.
verses.6:12: Now it came to pass in those days that He went out to the mountain to pray, and He continued through the night in prayer to God.
verses.6:13: And when day came, He called His disciples to Himself; and from them He chose twelve, whom He also named apostles:
verses.6:14: Simon, whom He also named Peter, and Andrew his brother, and James and John, and Philip and Bartholomew,
verses.6:15: and Matthew and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon who was called the Zealot,
verses.6:16: and Judas the son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.
verses.6:17: And coming down with them, He stood on a level place, together with a great crowd of His disciples and a great multitude of the people from all Judea and Jerusalem, and from the seacoast of Tyre and Sidon,
verses.6:18: who came to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases; and those who were troubled by unclean spirits were cured.
verses.6:19: And all the crowd sought to touch Him, for power was going forth from Him and healing them all.
verses.6:20: And raising His eyes toward His disciples, He said, "Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.
verses.6:21: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you shall be satisfied. Blessed are you who weep now, for you shall laugh.
verses.6:22: Blessed are you when men hate you, and when they exclude you, and reproach you, and cast out your name as evil on account of the Son of Man.
verses.6:23: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, for behold, your reward is great in heaven; for in like manner their fathers treated the prophets.
verses.6:24: Yet woe to you who are rich, for you have received your consolation in full.
verses.6:25: Woe to you who are full now, for you shall hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, for you shall mourn and weep.
verses.6:26: Woe when all men speak well of you, for in like manner their fathers treated the false prophets.
verses.6:27: But I say to you who hear: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,
verses.6:28: bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.
verses.6:29: To the one who strikes you on the cheek, present the other also; and from the one who takes your cloak, do not keep back your tunic as well.
verses.6:30: Give to all who ask of you, and from the one who takes what belongs to you, do not demand it back.
verses.6:31: And just as you desire that men should do to you, so do to them likewise.
verses.6:32: And if you love those who love you, what credit is yours? For even sinners love those who love them.
verses.6:33: For indeed if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is yours? Even sinners do the same.
verses.6:34: And if you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what credit is yours? Even sinners lend to sinners, that they may receive back an equal amount.
verses.6:35: Yet love your enemies, and do good, and lend, expecting nothing in return; and your reward shall be great, and you shall be sons of the Most High, for He Himself is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.
verses.6:36: Be compassionate, just as your Father is compassionate.
verses.6:37: And do not judge, and you shall by no means be judged; and do not condemn, and you shall by no means be condemned. Pardon, and you shall be pardoned;
verses.6:38: give, and it shall be given to you; a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and overflowing, they shall pour into your lap. For by the measure with which you measure, it shall be measured back to you."
verses.6:39: And He also spoke a parable to them: "Can a blind man guide a blind man? Will not both of them fall into a pit?
verses.6:40: A disciple is not above the teacher, yet everyone who is fully trained shall be like his teacher.
verses.6:41: And why do you look at the speck that is in your brother's eye, yet do not consider the beam that is in your own eye?
verses.6:42: How can you say to your brother, 'Brother, let me remove the speck that is in your eye,' when you yourself do not see the beam in your own eye? Hypocrite! First cast the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck that is in your brother's eye.
verses.6:43: For no good tree produces corrupt fruit, nor again does a corrupt tree produce good fruit.
verses.6:44: For each tree is known by its own fruit; for men do not gather figs from thorns, nor do they harvest grapes from a bramble bush.
verses.6:45: The good man out of the good treasure of the heart brings forth what is good, and the evil man out of evil brings forth what is evil; for out of the overflow of the heart his mouth speaks.
verses.6:46: Now why do you call Me, 'Lord, Lord,' and do not do what I say?
verses.6:47: As for everyone who comes to Me and hears My words and does them, I will show you whom he is like:
verses.6:48: he is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid a foundation upon the rock; and when a flood arose, the river dashed against that house, and could not shake it, because it had been well built.
verses.6:49: Yet the one who heard and did not act is like a man who built a house upon the ground without a foundation, against which the river dashed; and immediately it collapsed, and great was the ruin of that house."
verses.7:1: Now when He had completed all His words in the hearing of the people, He entered into Capernaum.
verses.7:2: And the servant of a certain centurion was sick and about to die, who was precious to him.
verses.7:3: When he heard of Jesus, he sent elders of the Jews to Him, requesting that He come and restore his servant to health.
verses.7:4: And having come to Jesus, they urged Him earnestly, saying, "He is worthy that You should grant him this,
verses.7:5: for he loves our nation, and he himself built the synagogue for us."
verses.7:6: So Jesus went along with them. And when He was already not far distant from the house, the centurion sent friends, saying to Him, "Lord, do not trouble Yourself, for I am not worthy that You should come under my roof.
verses.7:7: Therefore I did not even account myself worthy to come to You; only speak a word, and let my servant be healed.
verses.7:8: For I also am a man appointed under authority, having soldiers under me; and I say to this one, 'Go,' and he goes; and to another, 'Come,' and he comes; and to my servant, 'Do this,' and he does it."
verses.7:9: When Jesus heard these things, He marveled at him, and turning to the multitude following Him, He said, "I say to you, not even in Israel have I found so great a faith."
verses.7:10: And when those who had been sent returned to the house, they found the servant well.
verses.7:11: And it came to pass soon afterward that He journeyed to a city called Nain, and His disciples and a great multitude went with Him.
verses.7:12: As He drew near to the gate of the city, behold, a man who had died was being carried out—the only son of his mother, and she was a widow; and a sizable multitude from the city was with her.
verses.7:13: When the Lord saw her, He was moved with compassion for her and said to her, "Do not weep."
verses.7:14: Then He came forward and touched the bier, and those bearing it stood still. And He said, "Young man, I say to you, rise."
verses.7:15: And the dead man sat up and began to speak, and He gave him back to his mother.
verses.7:16: Then fear seized them all, and they glorified God, saying, "A great prophet has been raised up among us," and, "God has visited His people."
verses.7:17: And this report concerning Him went forth throughout all Judea and all the surrounding countryside.
verses.7:18: Then John's disciples brought word to him concerning all these things. And summoning two of his disciples, John
verses.7:19: sent them to Jesus, saying, "Are You the One who is to come, or should we look for another?"
verses.7:20: When the men came to Him, they said, "John the Baptist has sent us to You, saying, 'Are You the One who is to come, or should we look for another?'"
verses.7:21: In that very hour He healed many of sicknesses, afflictions, and evil spirits, and to many who were blind He graciously granted sight.
verses.7:22: And He answered and said to them, "Go and report to John the things which you have seen and heard: the blind recover sight, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have the gospel proclaimed to them.
verses.7:23: And blessed is the one who is not offended on account of Me."
verses.7:24: After the messengers of John had departed, He began to speak to the multitudes about John: "What did you go out into the wilderness to behold? A reed swayed by the wind?
verses.7:25: But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft garments? Behold, those who wear splendid attire and live in luxury are in royal palaces.
verses.7:26: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you, and far more than a prophet.
verses.7:27: This is he concerning whom it is written: 'Behold, I send forth My messenger before Your face, who shall prepare Your way before You.'
verses.7:28: I say to you, among those born of women no one is greater than John; yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he."
verses.7:29: (And all the people when they heard, including the tax collectors, vindicated God, having been baptized with the baptism of John;
verses.7:30: but the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected the counsel of God for themselves, not having been baptized by him.)
verses.7:31: "To what then shall I compare the people of this generation, and what are they like?
verses.7:32: They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another, who say, 'We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not weep.'
verses.7:33: For John the Baptist has come eating no bread and drinking no wine, and you say, 'He has a demon.'
verses.7:34: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, 'Behold, a gluttonous man and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'
verses.7:35: Yet wisdom is vindicated by all her children."
verses.7:36: Now one of the Pharisees invited Him to dine with him; and entering the Pharisee's house, He reclined at table.
verses.7:37: And behold, a woman of the city who was a sinner, upon learning that He was reclining at table in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster jar of fragrant ointment,
verses.7:38: and standing behind Him at His feet, weeping, she began to wet His feet with her tears and wiped them with the hair of her head; and she kept kissing His feet and anointing them with the ointment.
verses.7:39: Now when the Pharisee who had invited Him saw this, he said within himself, "If this Man were a prophet, He would know who and what sort of woman this is who touches Him, for she is a sinner."
verses.7:40: And Jesus answered him, "Simon, I have something to tell you." And he said, "Teacher, say it."
verses.7:41: "A certain moneylender had two debtors: one owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.
verses.7:42: Since they had nothing with which to pay, he graciously forgave them both. Which of them, therefore, will love him more?"
verses.7:43: Simon answered and said, "I suppose the one to whom he forgave the greater amount." And He said to him, "You have judged rightly."
verses.7:44: Then turning toward the woman, He said to Simon, "Do you see this woman? I entered your house; you did not give Me water for My feet, yet she has wet My feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
verses.7:45: You did not give Me a kiss; yet she, from the moment I came in, has not ceased kissing My feet.
verses.7:46: You did not anoint My head with oil; yet she has anointed My feet with fragrant ointment.
verses.7:47: Therefore I say to you, her many sins have been forgiven, for she has loved much; but the one who is forgiven little loves little."
verses.7:48: Then He said to her, "Your sins have been forgiven."
verses.7:49: And those reclining at table with Him began to say among themselves, "Who is this, who even forgives sins?"
verses.7:50: And He said to the woman, "Your faith has saved you; go forth in peace."
verses.8:1: Now it came to pass afterward that He journeyed through every city and village, proclaiming and bringing the glad tidings of the kingdom of God, and the twelve were with Him,
verses.8:2: and certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and infirmities: Mary, who was called Magdalene, out of whom seven demons had gone forth,
verses.8:3: and Joanna the wife of Chuza, Herod's steward, and Susanna, and many other women who ministered to them out of their own possessions.
verses.8:4: Now when a great multitude had gathered together, and people from every city were coming to Him, He spoke by a parable:
verses.8:5: "A sower went forth to sow his seed. And as he sowed, some fell beside the road, and it was trampled underfoot, and the birds of the air devoured it.
verses.8:6: And some fell upon the rock, and when it had sprung up, it withered away because it had no moisture.
verses.8:7: And some fell in the midst of the thorns, and the thorns sprang up together with it and choked it.
verses.8:8: And some fell into the good ground, and having sprung up, it bore fruit a hundredfold." As He spoke these things, He cried aloud, "He who has ears to hear, let him hear!"
verses.8:9: Then His disciples asked Him what this parable might mean.
verses.8:10: And He said, "To you it has been granted to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God, but to the rest it is in parables, so that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.
verses.8:11: Now this is the parable: The seed is the word of God.
verses.8:12: And those beside the road are they who have heard; then the devil comes and takes away the word from their heart, lest they should believe and be saved.
verses.8:13: And those upon the rock are they who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; yet these have no root, who believe for a season and in a time of testing fall away.
verses.8:14: And that which fell among the thorns—these are they who have heard, and as they go on their way they are choked by the cares and riches and pleasures of life, and they bring no fruit to maturity.
verses.8:15: And that in the good ground—these are they who, having heard the word with a noble and good heart, hold it fast and bear fruit with steadfast endurance.
verses.8:16: Now no one, when he has lighted a lamp, covers it with a vessel or sets it beneath a bed, but sets it upon a lampstand, so that those who enter may see the light.
verses.8:17: For there is nothing hidden that shall not become manifest, nor anything concealed that shall not be made known and come into the open.
verses.8:18: Take heed therefore how you hear; for whoever has, to him it shall be given, and whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has shall be taken away from him."
verses.8:19: Then His mother and His brethren came to Him, and they could not reach Him because of the multitude.
verses.8:20: And it was reported to Him, "Your mother and Your brethren are standing outside, desiring to see You."
verses.8:21: But He answered and said to them, "My mother and My brethren are these who hear the word of God and do it."
verses.8:22: Now it came to pass on one of those days that He went aboard a boat, He and His disciples, and He said to them, "Let us cross over to the other side of the lake." And they set sail.
verses.8:23: And as they sailed, He fell asleep. And a fierce windstorm swept down upon the lake, and they were filling with water and were in peril.
verses.8:24: And they came to Him and awakened Him, saying, "Master, Master, we are perishing!" Then He awoke and rebuked the wind and the surging of the water; and they ceased, and there came a calm.
verses.8:25: And He said to them, "Where is your faith?" And filled with fear, they marveled, saying to one another, "Who then is this, that He commands even the winds and the water, and they obey Him?"
verses.8:26: And they sailed to the country of the Gerasenes, which lies opposite Galilee.
verses.8:27: And when He stepped out onto the land, a certain man from the city met Him who had demons; and for a long time he had worn no clothing, nor did he abide in a house, but in the tombs.
verses.8:28: And when he saw Jesus, he cried out, fell down before Him, and with a loud voice said, "What have I to do with You, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I implore You, do not torment me!"
verses.8:29: For He had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For many times it had seized him, and he was kept under guard, bound with chains and shackles; yet tearing apart the bonds, he was driven by the demon into the desert places.
verses.8:30: And Jesus asked him, "What is your name?" And he said, "Legion," because many demons had entered into him.
verses.8:31: And they pleaded with Him not to command them to depart into the abyss.
verses.8:32: Now a large herd of swine was feeding there on the mountain, and they pleaded with Him to allow them to enter into them. And He gave them permission.
verses.8:33: Then the demons came out of the man and entered into the swine, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.
verses.8:34: And when those who tended them saw what had happened, they fled and reported it in the city and in the countryside.
verses.8:35: Then the people went out to see what had happened, and came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had departed sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed and in his right mind; and they were afraid.
verses.8:36: And those who had seen it reported to them how the man who had been demon-possessed was made well.
verses.8:37: Then the whole multitude of the surrounding region of the Gerasenes asked Him to depart from them, for they were seized with great fear. So He got into a boat and turned back.
verses.8:38: Now the man from whom the demons had gone out begged Him that he might be with Him; yet He sent him away, saying,
verses.8:39: "Return to your own house, and declare what great things God has done for you." And he went his way, proclaiming throughout the whole city what great things Jesus had done for him.
verses.8:40: Now as Jesus returned, the multitude welcomed Him, for they were all waiting for Him.
verses.8:41: And behold, there came a man named Jairus, and he was a ruler of the synagogue; and falling at the feet of Jesus, he pleaded with Him to come into his house,
verses.8:42: for he had an only daughter, about twelve years of age, and she was dying. Now as He went, the multitudes pressed closely around Him.
verses.8:43: And a woman who had a flow of blood for twelve years, who had spent all her livelihood upon physicians and could not be healed by any,
verses.8:44: came up from behind and touched the fringe of His garment, and immediately her flow of blood ceased.
verses.8:45: And Jesus said, "Who is the one who touched Me?" When all denied it, Peter said, "Master, the multitudes crowd around You and press upon You."
verses.8:46: But Jesus said, "Someone touched Me, for I perceived power going forth from Me."
verses.8:47: Now when the woman saw that she had not escaped notice, she came trembling, and falling down before Him, she declared before all the people for what reason she had touched Him and how she had been healed immediately.
verses.8:48: And He said to her, "Daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace."
verses.8:49: While He was still speaking, someone came from the house of the ruler of the synagogue, saying, "Your daughter has died; do not trouble the Teacher any longer."
verses.8:50: But when Jesus heard it, He answered him, "Do not fear; only believe, and she shall be made well."
verses.8:51: And when He came to the house, He permitted no one to go in with Him except Peter and John and James, and the father and mother of the child.
verses.8:52: Now all were weeping and mourning for her; but He said, "Do not weep, for she has not died, but is sleeping."
verses.8:53: And they laughed Him to scorn, knowing that she had died.
verses.8:54: But He took her by the hand and called aloud, saying, "Child, arise."
verses.8:55: And her spirit returned, and she arose immediately; and He directed that something be given her to eat.
verses.8:56: And her parents were astonished, yet He charged them to tell no one what had happened.
verses.9:1: Then having summoned the Twelve, He gave them power and authority over all the demons, and to cure diseases.
verses.9:2: And He sent them forth to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
verses.9:3: And He said to them, "Take nothing for the journey—neither staff, nor traveler's bag, nor bread, nor silver—nor are you to have two tunics.
verses.9:4: And into whatever house you enter, abide there, and depart from there.
verses.9:5: And as many as do not receive you, when you depart from that city, shake off the dust from your feet as a testimony against them."
verses.9:6: So departing, they passed through the villages, proclaiming the gospel and healing everywhere.
verses.9:7: Now Herod the tetrarch heard of all the things that were taking place, and he was deeply perplexed, because it was being said by some that John had been raised from the dead,
verses.9:8: and by some that Elijah had appeared, and by others that one of the ancient prophets had risen.
verses.9:9: And Herod said, "I myself beheaded John; yet who is this about whom I hear such things?" And he sought to see Him.
verses.9:10: And upon returning, the apostles recounted to Him all that they had done. And taking them with Him, He withdrew privately to a city called Bethsaida.
verses.9:11: But when the multitudes learned of it, they followed Him; and welcoming them, He spoke to them concerning the kingdom of God, and cured those who stood in need of healing.
verses.9:12: Now the day began to decline; and the Twelve approached and said to Him, "Dismiss the multitude, that they may go into the surrounding villages and countryside to lodge and find provisions, for here we are in a desolate place."
verses.9:13: But He said to them, "You yourselves give them something to eat." And they said, "We have no more than five loaves and two fish, unless we ourselves go and buy food for all this people."
verses.9:14: For there were about five thousand men. And He said to His disciples, "Have them recline in companies of about fifty each."
verses.9:15: And they did so, and had them all recline.
verses.9:16: Then taking the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up toward heaven, He blessed them and broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the multitude.
verses.9:17: And all ate and were filled, and what remained over to them was taken up—twelve baskets of broken pieces.
verses.9:18: And it came to pass, as He was praying alone, that the disciples were with Him; and He questioned them, saying, "Who do the multitudes say that I am?"
verses.9:19: And they answered and said, "John the Baptist; yet others say Elijah, and others that one of the ancient prophets has risen."
verses.9:20: Then He said to them, "But who do you yourselves say that I am?" And Peter answered and said, "The Christ of God."
verses.9:21: And strictly warning them, He commanded them to tell this to no one,
verses.9:22: saying, "The Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be slain, and on the third day be raised."
verses.9:23: And He was saying to all, "If anyone wishes to come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross day by day, and follow Me.
verses.9:24: For whoever wishes to save his life shall lose it; yet whoever loses his life on account of Me, that one shall save it.
verses.9:25: For how is a man profited if he gains the entire world, yet loses or forfeits his own self?
verses.9:26: For whoever is ashamed of Me and of My words, of that one the Son of Man shall be ashamed when He comes in His glory, and the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.
verses.9:27: Yet truly I say to you, there are some among those standing here who shall by no means taste death until they see the kingdom of God."
verses.9:28: Now it came to pass, about eight days after these sayings, that taking Peter and John and James with Him, He ascended the mountain to pray.
verses.9:29: And as He was praying, the appearance of His countenance became altered, and His apparel became dazzling white.
verses.9:30: And behold, two men were conversing with Him, who were Moses and Elijah,
verses.9:31: who appeared in glory and spoke of His departure, which He was about to fulfill in Jerusalem.
verses.9:32: Now Peter and those with him were weighed down with sleep; yet becoming fully awake, they beheld His glory and the two men who stood with Him.
verses.9:33: And it came to pass, as they were parting from Him, that Peter said to Jesus, "Master, it is good for us to be here; and let us make three tabernacles—one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah"—not knowing what he was saying.
verses.9:34: While he was speaking these things, a cloud came and overshadowed them; and they became fearful as they entered into the cloud.
verses.9:35: And a voice came forth from the cloud, saying, "This is My Son, the Chosen One; hear Him!"
verses.9:36: And when the voice had spoken, Jesus was found alone. And they kept silent, and in those days reported to no one anything of the things they had seen.
verses.9:37: Now it came to pass on the following day, when they had descended from the mountain, that a great multitude met Him.
verses.9:38: And behold, a man from the multitude cried out, saying, "Teacher, I implore You, look upon my son, for he is my only child;
verses.9:39: and behold, a spirit seizes him, and suddenly he cries out; and it convulses him with foaming, and scarcely departs from him, bruising him;
verses.9:40: and I implored Your disciples to cast it out, and they were not able."
verses.9:41: And answering, Jesus said, "O unbelieving and perverse generation, how long shall I remain with you and endure you? Bring your son here."
verses.9:42: And while he was still approaching, the demon dashed him down and violently convulsed him; but Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the boy, and restored him to his father.
verses.9:43: And all were astounded at the majesty of God. Yet while everyone was marveling at all the things which He was doing, He said to His disciples,
verses.9:44: "As for you, set these words in your ears, for the Son of Man is about to be delivered into the hands of men."
verses.9:45: But they did not comprehend this saying, and it was veiled from them so that they might not perceive it; and they were afraid to question Him concerning this saying.
verses.9:46: Then a dispute arose among them as to which of them might be the greatest.
verses.9:47: But Jesus, knowing the reasoning of their heart, took hold of a little child and set him beside Himself,
verses.9:48: and said to them, "Whoever welcomes this little child in My name welcomes Me, and whoever welcomes Me welcomes Him who sent Me; for he who is least among you all—that one is great."
verses.9:49: Now John answered and said, "Master, we saw someone casting out demons in Your name, and we tried to hinder him because he does not follow with us."
verses.9:50: But Jesus said to him, "Do not hinder him, for whoever is not against you is for you."
verses.9:51: Now it came to pass, as the days for His being taken up were drawing toward fulfillment, that He resolutely set His face to journey to Jerusalem,
verses.9:52: and sent messengers before His face. And going on, they entered a village of the Samaritans to make ready for Him;
verses.9:53: yet they did not welcome Him, because His face was set toward Jerusalem.
verses.9:54: And when the disciples James and John saw this, they said, "Lord, do You wish that we command fire to descend from heaven and consume them?"
verses.9:56: And they went on to another village.
verses.9:57: And as they were journeying along the way, someone said to Him, "I will follow You wherever You go."
verses.9:58: And Jesus said to him, "The foxes have dens and the birds of the sky have nests, yet the Son of Man has nowhere to rest His head."
verses.9:59: And He said to another, "Follow Me." But he said, "Lord, permit me first to go away and bury my father."
verses.9:60: But He said to him, "Leave the dead to bury their own dead; yet you, go forth and declare abroad the kingdom of God."
verses.9:61: And another also said, "I will follow You, Lord; yet first permit me to bid farewell to those at my house."
verses.9:62: But Jesus said, "No one who has laid his hand upon a plow and keeps looking back is fit for the kingdom of God."
verses.10:1: Now after these things the Lord appointed seventy-two others as well, and sent them two by two before His face into every city and place where He Himself was about to go.
verses.10:2: And He said to them, "The harvest indeed is abundant, yet the laborers are few; therefore pray to the Lord of the harvest that He may send forth laborers into His harvest.
verses.10:3: Go your way; behold, I am sending you forth as lambs in the midst of wolves.
verses.10:4: Carry no moneybag, no knapsack, and no sandals; and greet no one along the road.
verses.10:5: And into whatever house you enter, first say, 'Peace be to this house.'
verses.10:6: And if a son of peace is there, your peace shall rest upon him; but if not, it shall return to you.
verses.10:7: And remain in that same house, eating and drinking what is provided by them, for the laborer is worthy of his wages. Do not move from house to house.
verses.10:8: And into whatever city you enter and they receive you, eat the things set before you,
verses.10:9: and heal the sick who are in it, and say to them, 'The kingdom of God has drawn near to you.'
verses.10:10: Yet into whatever city you enter and they do not receive you, go out into its streets and say,
verses.10:11: 'Even the dust from your city that has clung to our feet we wipe off against you; nevertheless know this, that the kingdom of God has drawn near.'
verses.10:12: I say to you that on that day it shall be more bearable for Sodom than for that city.
verses.10:13: Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works done among you had been performed in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
verses.10:14: Yet it shall be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon in the judgment than for you.
verses.10:15: And you, Capernaum, will you be exalted to heaven? You shall descend to Hades!
verses.10:16: The one who hears you hears Me, and the one who rejects you rejects Me; and the one who rejects Me rejects Him who sent Me."
verses.10:17: Then the seventy-two returned with joy, saying, "Lord, even the demons are subject to us in Your name!"
verses.10:18: And He said to them, "I was watching Satan fall like lightning from heaven.
verses.10:19: Behold, I have given you authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means harm you.
verses.10:20: Nevertheless do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names have been written in the heavens."
verses.10:21: In that very hour He rejoiced greatly in the Holy Spirit and said, "I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because You have hidden these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to little children; yes, Father, for thus it was well-pleasing in Your sight.
verses.10:22: All things have been delivered to Me by My Father, and no one knows who the Son is except the Father, and who the Father is except the Son and the one to whom the Son wills to reveal Him."
verses.10:23: And turning to the disciples privately, He said, "Blessed are the eyes that see the things you see!
verses.10:24: For I say to you that many prophets and kings desired to see what you are seeing and did not see it, and to hear what you are hearing and did not hear it."
verses.10:25: And behold, a certain lawyer stood up, testing Him and saying, "Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?"
verses.10:26: And He said to him, "What is written in the law? How do you read it?"
verses.10:27: And answering, he said, "You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your strength, and with all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself."
verses.10:28: And He said to him, "You have answered rightly; do this, and you shall live."
verses.10:29: Yet he, desiring to justify himself, said to Jesus, "And who is my neighbor?"
verses.10:30: Jesus replied and said, "A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers, who both stripped him and beat him, and departed, leaving him half dead.
verses.10:31: Now by chance a certain priest was going down along that road, and when he saw him, he passed by on the opposite side.
verses.10:32: Likewise a Levite also, coming to that place and seeing him, passed by on the opposite side.
verses.10:33: But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came upon him; and seeing him, he was moved with compassion,
verses.10:34: and coming near, he bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine; and setting him upon his own animal, he brought him to an inn and cared for him.
verses.10:35: And on the next day, taking out two denarii, he gave them to the innkeeper and said, 'Care for him, and whatever more you spend, when I return I will repay you.'
verses.10:36: Which of these three, do you think, proved to be a neighbor to him who fell among the robbers?"
verses.10:37: And he said, "The one who showed mercy to him." Then Jesus said to him, "Go, and you also do likewise."
verses.10:38: Now as they went on their way, He entered a certain village; and a certain woman named Martha welcomed Him.
verses.10:39: And she had a sister called Mary, who also sat at the feet of Jesus and was listening to His word.
verses.10:40: But Martha was distracted with much serving; and she came up and said, "Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me alone to serve? Therefore tell her to help me."
verses.10:41: And the Lord answered and said to her, "Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things,
verses.10:42: yet few things are needed, or indeed one; for Mary has chosen the good portion, which shall not be taken away from her."
verses.11:1: And it came to pass, while He was praying in a certain place, that when He had finished, one of His disciples said to Him, "Lord, teach us to pray, just as John also taught his disciples."
verses.11:2: Then He said to them, "Whenever you pray, say, 'Father, hallowed be Your name; let Your kingdom come.
verses.11:3: Grant us our daily bread day by day.
verses.11:4: And forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone indebted to us; and do not bring us into temptation.'"
verses.11:5: And He said to them, "Which one of you shall have a friend, and go to him at midnight and say to him, 'Friend, lend me three loaves,
verses.11:6: since a friend of mine has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him';
verses.11:7: and he from within will answer and say, 'Do not cause me trouble; the door has already been shut, and my children are with me in bed; I cannot rise and give to you'?
verses.11:8: I say to you, even though he will not rise and give to him because he is his friend, yet because of his shameless persistence he will arise and give him as many as he needs.
verses.11:9: And I also say to you, ask, and it shall be given to you; seek, and you shall find; knock, and it shall be opened to you.
verses.11:10: For whoever asks receives, and he who seeks finds, and to him who knocks it shall be opened.
verses.11:11: Now which father among you, when his son asks for a fish, will give him a serpent instead of a fish?
verses.11:12: Or if he also asks for an egg, will he give him a scorpion?
verses.11:13: If you then, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more shall the Father from heaven give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him!"
verses.11:14: Now He was casting out a mute demon; and it came to pass, when the demon had gone out, that the mute man spoke, and the multitudes marveled.
verses.11:15: But some of them said, "By Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons, He casts out the demons."
verses.11:16: And others, testing Him, were seeking from Him a sign from heaven.
verses.11:17: But He, knowing their thoughts, said to them, "Every kingdom divided against itself is made desolate, and house falls upon house.
verses.11:18: And if Satan also is divided against himself, how shall his kingdom stand? For you say that I cast out the demons by Beelzebul.
verses.11:19: Yet if I cast out the demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they themselves shall be your judges.
verses.11:20: But if it is by the finger of God that I cast out the demons, then the kingdom of God has indeed come upon you.
verses.11:21: When the strong man, fully armed, guards his own palace, his possessions are in peace.
verses.11:22: But when one stronger than he comes upon him and overcomes him, he takes away his full armor in which he trusted, and distributes his spoils.
verses.11:23: The one who is not with Me is against Me, and the one who does not gather with Me scatters.
verses.11:24: When the unclean spirit goes out of a man, it passes through waterless places seeking rest; and finding none, it says, 'I will return to my house from which I came out.'
verses.11:25: And when it comes, it finds it swept and put in order.
verses.11:26: Then it goes and takes along seven other spirits more wicked than itself, and they enter in and dwell there; and the last state of that man becomes worse than the first."
verses.11:27: And it came to pass, as He spoke these things, that a certain woman from the multitude raised her voice and said to Him, "Blessed is the womb that bore You, and the breasts at which You nursed!"
verses.11:28: But He said, "Yes, rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it!"
verses.11:29: Now as the multitudes were crowding together, He began to say, "This generation is a wicked generation; it seeks a sign, and no sign shall be given to it except the sign of Jonah.
verses.11:30: For just as Jonah became a sign to the Ninevites, so also shall the Son of Man be to this generation.
verses.11:31: The queen of the South shall rise up at the judgment with the men of this generation and condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and behold, something greater than Solomon is here.
verses.11:32: The men of Nineveh shall stand up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the preaching of Jonah; and behold, something greater than Jonah is here.
verses.11:33: No one, when he has lit a lamp, places it in a hidden vault or under a measuring basket, but on the lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.
verses.11:34: Your eye is the lamp of the body. When your eye is sound, your whole body also is full of light; but when it is evil, your body also is full of darkness.
verses.11:35: Take heed therefore, lest the light within you be darkness.
verses.11:36: If then your whole body is full of light, having no part dark, it shall be wholly radiant, as when the lamp illuminates you with its bright rays."
verses.11:37: Now as He spoke, a Pharisee asked Him to dine with him; and He went in and reclined at table.
verses.11:38: And when the Pharisee saw it, he marveled that He had not first washed before the meal.
verses.11:39: Then the Lord said to him, "Now you Pharisees cleanse the outside of the cup and the dish, yet your inward part is full of extortion and wickedness.
verses.11:40: Foolish ones! Did not the One who made the outside make the inside also?
verses.11:41: Rather, give as alms those things that are within, and behold, all things are clean to you.
verses.11:42: But woe to you Pharisees! For you tithe mint and rue and every garden herb, yet pass by justice and the love of God. These you ought to have done, without neglecting the others.
verses.11:43: Woe to you Pharisees! For you love the foremost seat in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces.
verses.11:44: Woe to you! For you are like unmarked graves, and the men who walk over them do not know it."
verses.11:45: Then one of the lawyers answered and said to Him, "Teacher, in saying these things You insult us also."
verses.11:46: And He said, "Woe also to you lawyers! For you load men with burdens hard to bear, yet you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.
verses.11:47: Woe to you! For you build the tombs of the prophets, yet your fathers slew them.
verses.11:48: Therefore you are witnesses and consent to the deeds of your fathers; for they indeed slew them, and you build.
verses.11:49: For this reason also the wisdom of God said, 'I will send to them prophets and apostles, and some of them they will slay and persecute,'
verses.11:50: so that the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation,
verses.11:51: from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah, who perished between the altar and the house. Yes, I say to you, it shall be required of this generation!
verses.11:52: Woe to you lawyers! For you have taken away the key of knowledge; you did not enter in yourselves, and those who were entering in you hindered."
verses.11:53: And when He departed from there, the scribes and the Pharisees began to assail Him fiercely and to cross-examine Him about many things,
verses.11:54: lying in wait for Him, to catch something out of His mouth.
verses.12:1: Meanwhile, when tens of thousands of the multitude had gathered together, so that they trampled upon one another, He began to say to His disciples first, "Guard yourselves against the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
verses.12:2: Yet there is nothing covered over that shall not be revealed, and nothing hidden that shall not be known.
verses.12:3: Therefore, whatever you have said in the darkness shall be heard in the light, and what you have spoken into the ear in inner chambers shall be proclaimed upon the housetops.
verses.12:4: Now I say to you, My friends, do not be afraid of those who kill the body, and after these things have nothing further that they can do.
verses.12:5: But I will point out to you whom you should fear: fear Him who, after killing, has authority to cast into hell; yes, I say to you, fear Him!
verses.12:6: Are not five sparrows sold for two small copper coins? Yet not a single one of them is forgotten in the sight of God.
verses.12:7: Indeed, even all the hairs of your head have been numbered. Do not be afraid; you are of greater worth than many sparrows.
verses.12:8: Now I say to you, everyone who confesses Me before men, the Son of Man also shall confess him before the angels of God;
verses.12:9: but the one who denies Me in the presence of men shall be disowned in the presence of the angels of God.
verses.12:10: And everyone who shall speak a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; yet for the one who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven.
verses.12:11: Now when they bring you before the synagogues and the rulers and the authorities, do not be anxious about how or what you should speak in your defense, or what you should say;
verses.12:12: for the Holy Spirit shall teach you in that very hour the things you must say."
verses.12:13: Then someone from the multitude said to Him, "Teacher, instruct my brother to divide the inheritance with me."
verses.12:14: Yet He said to him, "Man, who appointed Me judge or divider over you?"
verses.12:15: Then He said to them, "Take heed and keep yourselves from all covetousness, for even when a person has an abundance, his life does not come from his possessions."
verses.12:16: And He spoke a parable to them, saying, "The land of a certain rich man yielded abundantly.
verses.12:17: And he reasoned within himself, saying, 'What shall I do, because I have nowhere to gather my crops?'
verses.12:18: And he said, 'This I will do: I will tear down my barns and build greater ones, and there I will gather all the grain and my goods.
verses.12:19: And I will say to my soul, "Soul, you have many good things stored up for many years; take your rest, eat, drink, and rejoice."'
verses.12:20: But God said to him, 'Fool! This very night your soul is demanded of you; and the things you have prepared, whose shall they be?'
verses.12:21: So it is with the one who stores up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God."
verses.12:22: And He said to His disciples, "Therefore I say to you, do not be anxious for your life, what you shall eat, nor for your body, what you shall put on.
verses.12:23: For life is greater than food, and the body greater than clothing.
verses.12:24: Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, they have neither storeroom nor barn, yet God nourishes them. How much greater is your worth than that of the birds!
verses.12:25: And which of you by being anxious is able to add a cubit to his span of life?
verses.12:26: If then you are unable to do even the smallest thing, why are you anxious about the rest?
verses.12:27: Consider how the lilies grow: they neither labor nor spin; yet I say to you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
verses.12:28: But if God thus clothes the grass that is in the field today and tomorrow is cast into the oven, how much more shall He clothe you, you of little faith!
verses.12:29: And as for you, do not seek what you shall eat and what you shall drink, nor be kept in anxious suspense.
