verses.12:30: For all these things the nations of the world eagerly seek, and your Father knows that you have need of these things.
verses.12:31: Rather, seek His kingdom, and these things shall be added to you.
verses.12:32: Do not be afraid, little flock, for your Father has been well pleased to give you the kingdom.
verses.12:33: Sell your possessions and give alms; make for yourselves purses that do not wear out, an unfailing treasure in the heavens, where no thief draws near and no moth destroys.
verses.12:34: For wherever your treasure is, there also your heart shall be.
verses.12:35: Keep your loins girded and your lamps burning,
verses.12:36: and be like men waiting for their master to return from the wedding banquet, so that when he comes and knocks, they may open to him at once.
verses.12:37: Blessed are those servants whom the master, upon his coming, shall find keeping watch. Assuredly, I say to you, he will gird himself and have them recline at table, and coming forward, he will serve them.
verses.12:38: And even if he comes in the second watch, or in the third watch, and finds them so, blessed are they!
verses.12:39: Now know this: if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have permitted his house to be broken into.
verses.12:40: You also must be ready, for at an hour you do not expect, the Son of Man is coming."
verses.12:41: Then Peter said, "Lord, are You speaking this parable to us, or also to all?"
verses.12:42: And the Lord said, "Who then is the faithful and prudent steward, whom the master shall appoint over his household, to give them their allowance of food at the proper time?
verses.12:43: Blessed is that servant whom his master, upon his coming, shall find doing so.
verses.12:44: Truly, I say to you, he shall appoint him over all his possessions.
verses.12:45: Yet if that servant says in his heart, 'My master delays his coming,' and begins to strike the menservants and maidservants, and to eat and drink and grow drunk,
verses.12:46: the master of that servant will come on a day when he does not expect him and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in two and assign his portion with the unfaithful.
verses.12:47: And that servant who knew his master's will, yet did not make ready or act according to his will, shall be beaten with many blows;
verses.12:48: but the one who did not know, yet did things worthy of blows, shall be beaten with few. For to everyone to whom much was given, from him much shall be required; and to the one to whom much was entrusted, of him they will demand even more.
verses.12:49: I have come to cast fire upon the earth, and how I long that it were already kindled!
verses.12:50: Yet I have a baptism to be baptized with, and how greatly I am constrained until it is brought to completion!
verses.12:51: Do you imagine that I came to give peace upon the earth? No, I say to you, but rather division.
verses.12:52: For from now on, five in one household shall be divided, three against two and two against three;
verses.12:53: they shall be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against mother, mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law and daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law."
verses.12:54: Then He also said to the multitudes, "Whenever you see a cloud rising in the west, at once you say, 'A rainstorm is coming,' and so it comes to pass.
verses.12:55: And when a south wind is blowing, you say, 'There will be scorching heat,' and so it happens.
verses.12:56: Hypocrites! You know how to discern the appearance of the earth and of the sky, yet how is it that you do not know how to discern this present time?
verses.12:57: And why do you not also judge for yourselves what is right?
verses.12:58: For as you go with your adversary before a magistrate, take pains along the way to be released from him, lest he drag you to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer cast you into prison.
verses.12:59: I say to you, you shall by no means come out from there until you have paid even the very last mite."
verses.13:1: Now at that very time some were present who brought Him word concerning the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices.
verses.13:2: And in answer He said to them, "Do you suppose that these Galileans were greater sinners than all other Galileans because they have suffered these things?
verses.13:3: No, I say to you; rather, unless you repent, you shall all likewise perish.
verses.13:4: Or those eighteen upon whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them—do you suppose that they were greater offenders than all the people who dwell in Jerusalem?
verses.13:5: No, I say to you; rather, unless you repent, you shall all perish in the same manner."
verses.13:6: Then He spoke this parable: "A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit upon it and found none.
verses.13:7: And he said to the vinedresser, 'Behold, for three years I have been coming seeking fruit on this fig tree, and I find none. Cut it down! Why does it even exhaust the ground?'
verses.13:8: But in answer he said to him, 'Sir, leave it alone this year also, until I dig around it and put manure on it;
verses.13:9: and if it bears fruit in the time to come—but if not, you shall cut it down.'"
verses.13:10: Now He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
verses.13:11: And behold, there was a woman who had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years; she was bent over and altogether unable to straighten herself up.
verses.13:12: When Jesus saw her, He called her forward and said to her, "Woman, you are set free from your infirmity."
verses.13:13: And He laid His hands upon her, and immediately she was made straight and began glorifying God.
verses.13:14: But the ruler of the synagogue, indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, answered and said to the multitude, "There are six days in which work ought to be done; therefore come and be healed on those days, and not on the day of the Sabbath."
verses.13:15: Then the Lord answered him and said, "Hypocrites! Does not each of you on the Sabbath loose his ox or donkey from the manger and lead it away to water it?
verses.13:16: And ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham whom Satan has bound—behold, for eighteen years—to be loosed from this bond on the Sabbath day?"
verses.13:17: And as He was saying these things, all His adversaries were put to shame; and the entire multitude rejoiced over all the glorious deeds that were being done by Him.
verses.13:18: Therefore He said, "What is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it?
verses.13:19: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and cast into his own garden; and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches."
verses.13:20: And again He said, "To what shall I compare the kingdom of God?
verses.13:21: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until the whole of it was leavened."
verses.13:22: And He went on His way through cities and villages, teaching and making His journey toward Jerusalem.
verses.13:23: Then someone said to Him, "Lord, are there only a few who are being saved?" And He said to them,
verses.13:24: "Strive to enter through the narrow door, for many, I tell you, will seek to enter and will not be able.
verses.13:25: Once the Master of the house has risen and shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying, 'Lord, open to us!' He will answer and say to you, 'I do not know you, where you are from.'
verses.13:26: Then you will begin to say, 'We ate and drank in Your presence, and You taught in our streets.'
verses.13:27: And He will speak, saying to you, 'I do not know where you are from. Depart from Me, all you workers of iniquity!'
verses.13:28: There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, and yourselves cast outside.
verses.13:29: And people shall come from east and west, and from north and south, and shall recline at table in the kingdom of God.
verses.13:30: And behold, there are last who shall be first, and there are first who shall be last."
verses.13:31: At that very hour some Pharisees came up, saying to Him, "Depart and go away from here, for Herod desires to kill You."
verses.13:32: And He said to them, "Go and tell that fox, 'Behold, I cast out demons and perform healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I reach completion.'
verses.13:33: Nevertheless, I must journey on today and tomorrow and the day following, for it cannot be that a prophet should perish outside of Jerusalem.
verses.13:34: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those who have been sent to her—how often I desired to gather your children together, just as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!
verses.13:35: Behold, your house is left to you. And I say to you, you shall by no means see Me until the time comes when you say, 'Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!'"
verses.14:1: Now it came to pass, when He went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, that they were watching Him closely.
verses.14:2: And behold, there was a certain man before Him who had dropsy.
verses.14:3: And Jesus answered and spoke to the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, "Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath, or not?"
verses.14:4: But they remained silent. And taking hold of him, He healed him and sent him away.
verses.14:5: Then He said to them, "Which of you, having a son or an ox that falls into a well, will not immediately pull him up on the Sabbath day?"
verses.14:6: And they were not able to answer back to these things.
verses.14:7: Now He told a parable to those who were invited, observing how they were choosing the places of honor, saying to them,
verses.14:8: "When you are invited by anyone to a wedding feast, do not recline in the place of honor, lest someone more honorable than you has been invited by him;
verses.14:9: and he who invited both you and him will come and say to you, 'Give place to this man,' and then with shame you will begin to occupy the lowest place.
verses.14:10: Rather, when you are invited, go and recline in the lowest place, so that when he who invited you comes, he may say to you, 'Friend, move up higher.' Then you shall have honor in the presence of all those who recline at table with you.
verses.14:11: For everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled, and he who humbles himself shall be exalted."
verses.14:12: Then He also said to the one who had invited Him, "When you prepare a midday meal or a dinner, do not summon your friends, nor your brothers, nor your relatives, nor wealthy neighbors, lest they also invite you in return and repayment be made to you.
verses.14:13: Rather, when you give a feast, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind;
verses.14:14: and you shall be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you; for you shall be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous."
verses.14:15: Now when one of those reclining at table heard these things, he said to Him, "Blessed is he who shall eat bread in the kingdom of God!"
verses.14:16: But He said to him, "A certain man was preparing a great banquet and invited many,
verses.14:17: and at the hour of the banquet he sent his servant to say to those who had been invited, 'Come, for things are now ready.'
verses.14:18: Yet all alike began with one accord to make excuses. The first said to him, 'I have bought a field, and I must go out and inspect it; I ask you, consider me excused.'
verses.14:19: And another said, 'I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am on my way to test them; I ask you, consider me excused.'
verses.14:20: And still another said, 'I have married a wife, and for this reason I am not able to come.'
verses.14:21: So the servant returned and reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house, being angry, said to his servant, 'Go out swiftly into the broad streets and alleys of the city, and bring in here the poor and the crippled and the blind and the lame.'
verses.14:22: And the servant said, 'Master, what you commanded has been done, and still there is room.'
verses.14:23: And the master said to the servant, 'Go out into the roads and hedges, and compel people to come in, so that my house may be filled;
verses.14:24: for I tell you that not one of those men who were invited shall taste of my banquet.'"
verses.14:25: Now great multitudes were journeying along with Him, and turning around He said to them,
verses.14:26: "If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his own father and mother, and wife and children, and brothers and sisters, yes, and even his own life, he cannot be My disciple.
verses.14:27: Whoever does not carry his cross and come after Me cannot be My disciple.
verses.14:28: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the cost, to see whether he has enough to complete it?
verses.14:29: Otherwise, when he has laid a foundation and is not able to finish, all who behold it will begin to mock him,
verses.14:30: saying, 'This man began to build and was not able to finish.'
verses.14:31: Or what king, marching out to encounter another king in war, will not first sit down and take counsel whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one who comes against him with twenty thousand?
verses.14:32: And if not, while the other is still far off, he sends a delegation and asks for terms of peace.
verses.14:33: So therefore, every one of you who does not renounce all his own possessions cannot be My disciple.
verses.14:34: Therefore salt is good; yet if even the salt loses its savor, with what shall it be seasoned?
verses.14:35: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile; they cast it out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear."
verses.15:1: Now all the tax collectors and the sinners were drawing near to Him to listen to Him.
verses.15:2: And both the Pharisees and the scribes were grumbling, saying, "This Man welcomes sinners and eats with them."
verses.15:3: Then He told this parable to them, saying:
verses.15:4: "What man among you, having one hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the lost one until he finds it?
verses.15:5: And having found it, he places it upon his shoulders, rejoicing.
verses.15:6: And coming to his house, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep that was lost!'
verses.15:7: I say to you that in this way there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous ones who have no need of repentance.
verses.15:8: Or what woman, having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp and sweep the house and search diligently until she finds it?
verses.15:9: And having found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, 'Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma that I lost!'
verses.15:10: In the same way, I say to you, there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents."
verses.15:11: And He said, "A certain man had two sons.
verses.15:12: And the younger of them said to his father, 'Father, give me the share of the property that falls to me.' And he divided his living between them.
verses.15:13: And not many days later, the younger son gathered everything together and departed to a distant country, and there he squandered his estate, living dissolutely.
verses.15:14: And when he had spent everything, a severe famine arose throughout that country, and he began to be in need.
verses.15:15: So he went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, and that man sent him into his fields to tend swine.
verses.15:16: And he longed to be filled with the carob pods that the swine were eating, and no one gave anything to him.
verses.15:17: But coming to himself, he said, 'How many hired laborers of my father have bread in abundance, while I am perishing here with hunger!
verses.15:18: I will arise and go to my father, and I will say to him, "Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you;
verses.15:19: I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Make me like one of your hired laborers."'
verses.15:20: So he rose up and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was moved with compassion; and he ran and fell upon his neck and kissed him tenderly.
verses.15:21: And the son said to him, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you; I am no longer worthy to be called your son.'
verses.15:22: But the father said to his servants, 'Quickly bring out the finest robe and clothe him with it, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet;
verses.15:23: and bring the fattened calf and slay it, and let us eat and make merry;
verses.15:24: for this son of mine was dead and has come to life again; he was lost and has been found.' And they began to make merry.
verses.15:25: Now his elder son was in the field; and as he came and approached the house, he heard music and dancing.
verses.15:26: And calling one of the servants to himself, he inquired what these things might mean.
verses.15:27: And he said to him, 'Your brother has come, and your father has slain the fattened calf because he has received him back safe and sound.'
verses.15:28: But he became angry and was unwilling to go in. Therefore his father came out and pleaded with him.
verses.15:29: But answering, he said to his father, 'Behold, for so many years I have served you, and I have never transgressed a commandment of yours; yet to me you never gave a young goat, that I might make merry with my friends.
verses.15:30: Yet when this son of yours came, who has devoured your livelihood with harlots, you slew the fattened calf for him.'
verses.15:31: And he said to him, 'Child, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.
verses.15:32: Yet it was fitting to make merry and be glad, for this brother of yours was dead and is alive, and was lost and has been found.'"
verses.16:1: Now He was also saying to the disciples, "There was a certain rich man who had a steward, and this man was accused to him of squandering his possessions.
verses.16:2: And calling him, he said to him, 'What is this I hear concerning you? Render the account of your stewardship, for you can no longer be steward.'
verses.16:3: Then the steward said within himself, 'What shall I do, since my master is taking the stewardship away from me? I do not have the strength to dig; I am ashamed to beg.
verses.16:4: I have decided what I will do, so that when I am removed from the stewardship, they may welcome me into their houses.'
verses.16:5: So summoning each one of his master's debtors, he said to the first, 'How much do you owe my master?'
verses.16:6: And he said, 'One hundred baths of oil.' Then he said to him, 'Take your bill, sit down quickly, and write fifty.'
verses.16:7: Next he said to another, 'And how much do you owe?' And he said, 'One hundred kors of wheat.' He said to him, 'Take your bill and write eighty.'
verses.16:8: And the master commended the unrighteous steward because he had acted shrewdly; for the sons of this age are more shrewd toward their own generation than the sons of light.
verses.16:9: And I say to you, make friends for yourselves by means of unrighteous mammon, so that when it fails, they may welcome you into the eternal dwellings.
verses.16:10: Whoever is faithful in a very small matter is faithful also in much, and whoever is unrighteous in a very small matter is unrighteous also in much.
verses.16:11: Therefore, if you have not proven faithful in unrighteous mammon, who will entrust to you that which is true?
verses.16:12: And if you have not proven faithful in what belongs to another, who will give to you what is your own?
verses.16:13: No household servant is able to serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon."
verses.16:14: Now the Pharisees, who were lovers of money, were listening to all these things, and they were scoffing at Him.
verses.16:15: And He said to them, "You are the ones who justify yourselves in the sight of men, but God knows your hearts; for that which is exalted among men is an abomination before God.
verses.16:16: The Law and the Prophets were until John; from that time the kingdom of God is proclaimed as good news, and everyone presses forcefully into it.
verses.16:17: Yet it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one stroke of a letter of the Law to fall.
verses.16:18: Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and he who marries one divorced from a husband commits adultery.
verses.16:19: Now there was a certain rich man, and he dressed in purple and fine linen, feasting sumptuously every day.
verses.16:20: And a certain poor man named Lazarus, covered with sores, had been laid at his gate,
verses.16:21: and longing to be filled from what fell from the rich man's table; moreover, even the dogs came and licked his sores.
verses.16:22: Now it came to pass that the poor man died and was carried away by the angels into Abraham's bosom. The rich man also died and was buried.
verses.16:23: And in Hades, lifting up his eyes while being in torments, he saw Abraham from afar and Lazarus in his bosom.
verses.16:24: And crying out, he said, 'Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus so that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue; for I am in agony in this flame.'
verses.16:25: But Abraham said, 'Child, remember that in your lifetime you received your good things, and Lazarus likewise bad things; yet now he is comforted here, while you are in agony.
verses.16:26: And besides all this, between us and you a great chasm has been firmly fixed, so that those who wish to cross over from here to you are not able, nor can any pass from there to us.'
verses.16:27: Then he said, 'Therefore I beg you, father, that you send him to my father's house,
verses.16:28: for I have five brothers, so that he may solemnly warn them, lest they also come into this place of torment.'
verses.16:29: But Abraham said, 'They have Moses and the Prophets; let them listen to them.'
verses.16:30: And he said, 'No, father Abraham; rather, if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent.'
verses.16:31: But he said to him, 'If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, neither will they be persuaded even if someone rises from the dead.'"
verses.17:1: Then He said to His disciples, "It is impossible that occasions of stumbling should not come, yet woe to the one through whom they come.
verses.17:2: It would profit him more if a millstone were hung around his neck and he were cast into the sea, than that he should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
verses.17:3: Keep watch over yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.
verses.17:4: And if seven times in the day he sins against you, and seven times returns to you, saying, 'I repent,' you shall forgive him."
verses.17:5: And the apostles said to the Lord, "Add to our faith."
verses.17:6: Then the Lord said, "If you have faith like a grain of mustard seed, you would say to this mulberry tree, 'Be uprooted and planted in the sea,' and it would obey you.
verses.17:7: And which of you, having a servant plowing or tending sheep, will say to him when he comes in from the field, 'Come at once and recline at table,'
verses.17:8: and will not instead say to him, 'Prepare what I shall eat for supper, and gird yourself and wait on me until I have eaten and drunk; and after that you yourself shall eat and drink'?
verses.17:9: Does he give thanks to the servant because he did the things commanded?
verses.17:10: In the same way you also, when you have carried out all the things commanded you, say, 'We are unprofitable servants; we have performed what it was our duty to do.'"
verses.17:11: And it came to pass, as He was journeying to Jerusalem, that He passed between Samaria and Galilee.
verses.17:12: And as He was entering a certain village, ten leprous men met Him, who stood afar off.
verses.17:13: And they raised their voices, saying, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!"
verses.17:14: And seeing them, He said to them, "Go and show yourselves to the priests." And it came to pass that while they were going, they were cleansed.
verses.17:15: Now one of them, seeing that he had been healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice,
verses.17:16: and he fell upon his face at His feet, giving thanks to Him; and he was a Samaritan.
verses.17:17: Then Jesus answered and said, "Were not the ten cleansed? Where, then, are the nine?
verses.17:18: Were none found who turned back to give glory to God except this foreigner?"
verses.17:19: Then He said to him, "Rise and go your way; your faith has made you whole."
verses.17:20: Now being questioned by the Pharisees as to when the kingdom of God is coming, He answered them and said, "The kingdom of God does not come with observation,
verses.17:21: nor shall they say, 'Behold, here!' or, 'There!' For behold, the kingdom of God is within you."
verses.17:22: Then He said to the disciples, "Days will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you shall not see it.
verses.17:23: And they will say to you, 'Behold, there!' or, 'Behold, here!' Do not go out, nor pursue them.
verses.17:24: For just as the lightning flashes from one end under heaven and shines to the other end under heaven, so shall the Son of Man be in His day.
verses.17:25: First, however, He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
verses.17:26: And just as it came to pass in the days of Noah, so shall it also be in the days of the Son of Man:
verses.17:27: they were eating, drinking, marrying, being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark, and the flood came and destroyed all of them.
verses.17:28: Likewise, just as it came to pass in the days of Lot: they were eating, drinking, buying, selling, planting, building;
verses.17:29: yet on the day Lot departed from Sodom, it rained fire and brimstone from heaven and destroyed all of them.
verses.17:30: Just so shall it be on the day that the Son of Man is revealed.
verses.17:31: On that day, let the one who is upon the housetop, whose belongings are in the house, not come down to carry them off; and likewise let the one who is in the field not turn back to what is behind.
verses.17:33: Whoever seeks to preserve his life shall lose it, and whoever loses it shall keep it alive.
verses.17:34: I say to you, on that night there shall be two upon one bed: one shall be taken, and the other shall be left;
verses.17:35: there shall be two women grinding together: one shall be taken, and the other shall be left."
verses.17:37: And answering, they said to Him, "Where, Lord?" And He said to them, "Where the body is, there also shall the eagles be gathered together."
verses.18:1: Now He spoke a parable to them that they ought to pray at all times and not grow faint,
verses.18:2: saying, "In a certain city there was a judge who did not fear God and had no regard for man.
verses.18:3: And in that city there was a widow, and she kept coming to him, saying, 'Vindicate me against my adversary.'
verses.18:4: And for a time he was unwilling; yet afterward he said within himself, 'Even though I do not fear God nor have regard for man,
verses.18:5: yet because this widow causes me trouble, I will vindicate her, lest by coming continually she wear me down.'"
verses.18:6: Then the Lord said, "Hear what the unjust judge says.
verses.18:7: And shall God not bring about vindication for His elect who cry out to Him day and night, even though He bears long over them?
verses.18:8: I say to you that He will bring about their vindication swiftly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will He indeed find faith upon the earth?"
verses.18:9: And He also spoke this parable to certain ones who trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and held the rest in contempt:
verses.18:10: "Two men went up to the temple to pray, the one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
verses.18:11: The Pharisee stood and prayed these things to himself: 'O God, I give thanks to You that I am not like the rest of men—extortioners, unrighteous, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.
verses.18:12: I fast twice a week; I pay tithes on all that I acquire.'
verses.18:13: But the tax collector, standing at a distance, was unwilling even to lift up his eyes to heaven, but kept beating his breast, saying, 'O God, be merciful to me, the sinner!'
verses.18:14: I say to you, this man went down to his house justified rather than that one; for everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled, and the one who humbles himself shall be exalted."
verses.18:15: Now they were bringing even infants to Him that He might touch them; and when the disciples saw this, they rebuked them.
verses.18:16: But Jesus called them to Himself, saying, "Let the little children come to Me, and do not hinder them; for to such as these belongs the kingdom of God.
verses.18:17: Assuredly, I say to you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child shall never enter into it."
verses.18:18: And a certain ruler questioned Him, saying, "Good Teacher, what must I do that I may inherit eternal life?"
verses.18:19: Then Jesus said to him, "Why do you call Me good? None is good except One alone—God.
verses.18:20: You know the commandments: 'Do not commit adultery; Do not murder; Do not steal; Do not bear false witness; Honor your father and mother.'"
verses.18:21: And he replied, "I have kept all these things from my youth."
verses.18:22: When Jesus heard this, He said to him, "One thing you still lack: sell everything you possess and distribute to the poor, and you shall have treasure in the heavens; and come, follow Me."
verses.18:23: But when he heard these things, he became deeply sorrowful, for he was exceedingly wealthy.
verses.18:24: And looking at him, Jesus said, "How difficult it is for those who possess wealth to enter into the kingdom of God!
verses.18:25: For it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God."
verses.18:26: And those who heard said, "Who then is able to be saved?"
verses.18:27: But He said, "The things impossible with men are possible with God."
verses.18:28: Then Peter said, "Behold, we have left all things and have followed You."
verses.18:29: And He said to them, "Assuredly, I say to you that there is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children on account of the kingdom of God,
verses.18:30: who shall not receive manifold more in this present time, and in the coming age, eternal life."
verses.18:31: Then taking the twelve aside, He said to them, "Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things written through the prophets concerning the Son of Man shall be accomplished.
verses.18:32: For He shall be handed over to the Gentiles, and shall be mocked and shamefully treated and spat upon;
verses.18:33: and after scourging Him, they shall put Him to death; and on the third day He shall rise again."
verses.18:34: Yet they understood none of these things; and this saying was concealed from them, and they did not grasp what was being spoken.
verses.18:35: Now it came to pass, as He drew near to Jericho, that a certain blind man was sitting beside the road begging.
verses.18:36: And hearing a multitude passing by, he inquired what this might be.
verses.18:37: And they reported to him that Jesus the Nazarene was passing by.
verses.18:38: And he cried aloud, saying, "Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!"
verses.18:39: And those who were going ahead rebuked him that he should keep silent; yet he cried out all the more, "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
verses.18:40: Then Jesus stopped and commanded that he be brought to Him; and when he had drawn near, He questioned him,
verses.18:41: "What do you want Me to do for you?" And he said, "Lord, that I may regain my sight."
verses.18:42: And Jesus said to him, "Regain your sight; your faith has saved you."
verses.18:43: And immediately he regained his sight and began following Him, glorifying God; and when all the people saw it, they gave praise to God.
verses.19:1: And having entered, He was passing through Jericho.
verses.19:2: And behold, there was a man called by name Zacchaeus, and he was a chief tax collector, and he was wealthy.
verses.19:3: And he was seeking to see Jesus, who He was, and could not because of the multitude, for he was small in stature.
verses.19:4: And running on ahead, he climbed up into a sycamore-fig tree to see Him, for He was about to pass that way.
verses.19:5: And when Jesus came to the place, He looked up and said to him, "Zacchaeus, hasten and come down, for today I must abide at your house."
verses.19:6: And he hastened and came down, and welcomed Him with joy.
verses.19:7: And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, "He has gone in to lodge with a sinful man."
verses.19:8: Then Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, "Behold, Lord, half of my possessions I give to the poor, and if I have defrauded anyone of anything, I repay it fourfold."
verses.19:9: And Jesus said to him, "This day salvation has come to this house, since he too is a son of Abraham;
verses.19:10: for the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which is lost."
verses.19:11: Now as they were listening to these things, He went on to speak a parable, because He was near Jerusalem and they supposed that the kingdom of God was about to appear immediately.
verses.19:12: Therefore He said, "A certain man of noble birth journeyed to a distant country to receive a kingdom for himself and to return.
verses.19:13: And calling ten of his own servants, he gave them ten minas and said to them, 'Engage in trade until I come.'
verses.19:14: But his citizens hated him, and sent an embassy after him, saying, 'We do not want this man to reign over us.'
verses.19:15: And it came to pass, when he returned after receiving the kingdom, that he commanded these servants to whom he had given the money to be summoned to him, so that he might know what they had gained by trading.
verses.19:16: Then the first came before him, saying, 'Master, your mina has gained ten more minas.'
verses.19:17: And he said to him, 'Well done, good servant! Because you proved faithful in a very little, hold authority over ten cities.'
verses.19:18: And the second came, saying, 'Your mina, Master, has made five minas.'
verses.19:19: And to this one also he said, 'You also be over five cities.'
verses.19:20: And the other came, saying, 'Master, behold your mina, which I kept laid away in a handkerchief;
verses.19:21: for I feared you, because you are a severe man: you take up what you did not lay down, and you reap what you did not sow.'
verses.19:22: He says to him, 'Out of your own mouth I judge you, wicked servant! Did you know that I am a severe man, taking up what I did not lay down and reaping what I did not sow?
verses.19:23: Why then did you not place my money in the bank? Then at my coming I would have collected it with interest.'
verses.19:24: And he said to those standing by, 'Take the mina from him and give it to the one who has the ten minas'—
verses.19:25: and they said to him, 'Master, he has ten minas'—
verses.19:26: 'I say to you that to everyone who has, it shall be given; but from the one who does not have, even what he has shall be taken away.
verses.19:27: But as for these enemies of mine, who did not want me to reign over them, bring them here and slay them before me.'"
verses.19:28: And having spoken these things, He went on ahead, ascending to Jerusalem.
verses.19:29: And it came to pass, as He drew near to Bethphage and Bethany, toward the mount called Olivet, that He sent two of the disciples,
verses.19:30: saying, "Go into the village opposite you; upon entering it, you shall find a colt tied, on which no man has ever sat. Untie it and bring it.
verses.19:31: And if anyone asks you, 'Why are you untying it?' thus you shall say: 'The Lord has need of it.'"
verses.19:32: So those who had been sent departed and found it just as He had told them.
verses.19:33: And as they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, "Why are you untying the colt?"
verses.19:34: And they said, "The Lord has need of it."
verses.19:35: And they brought it to Jesus; and casting their own garments upon the colt, they set Jesus upon it.
verses.19:36: And as He went along, they spread their garments on the road.
verses.19:37: And as He was now approaching the descent of the Mount of Olives, the entire multitude of the disciples began to rejoice and to praise God with a loud voice for all the mighty works that they had seen,
verses.19:38: saying, "Blessed is He who comes, the King, in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest!"
verses.19:39: And some of the Pharisees from the multitude said to Him, "Teacher, rebuke Your disciples."
verses.19:40: And answering, He said, "I say to you that if these keep silent, the stones shall cry out."
verses.19:41: And as He drew near and beheld the city, He wept over it,
verses.19:42: saying, "If only you, even you, had known in this day the things that belong to peace—but now they have been hidden from your eyes.
verses.19:43: For days shall come upon you when your enemies shall raise a barricade around you, and encircle you, and hem you in on every side,
verses.19:44: and they shall dash you to the ground, and your children within you, and they shall not leave one stone upon another within you, because you did not recognize the time of your visitation."
verses.19:45: And having entered into the temple, He began to cast out those who were selling,
verses.19:46: saying to them, "It is written, 'My house is a house of prayer,' but you have made it a den of robbers."
verses.19:47: And He was teaching daily in the temple; yet the chief priests and the scribes were seeking to destroy Him, along with the leading men of the people,
verses.19:48: and they could not find what they might do, for all the people hung upon Him, listening.
verses.20:1: And it came to pass on one of the days, as He was teaching the people in the temple and proclaiming the gospel, that the chief priests and the scribes, together with the elders, came upon Him,
verses.20:2: and spoke to Him, saying, "Tell us by what authority You do these things, or who is the one who gave You this authority?"
verses.20:3: And He answered and said to them, "I will also ask you a question; tell Me:
verses.20:4: Was the baptism of John from heaven or from men?"
verses.20:5: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, "If we say, 'From heaven,' He will say, 'Why did you not believe him?'
verses.20:6: But if we say, 'From men,' all the people will stone us to death, for they are persuaded that John was a prophet."
verses.20:7: And they answered that they did not know where it came from.
verses.20:8: And Jesus said to them, "Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things."
verses.20:9: Then He began to speak this parable to the people: "A man planted a vineyard, leased it to vinedressers, and departed abroad for a long time.
verses.20:10: And in due season he sent a servant to the vinedressers, that they should give him some of the fruit of the vineyard; but the vinedressers beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
verses.20:11: And he proceeded to send another servant; but they beat that one also, dishonored him, and sent him away empty-handed.
verses.20:12: And he proceeded to send a third; but this one also they wounded and cast out.
verses.20:13: Then the master of the vineyard said, 'What shall I do? I will send my beloved son; perhaps they will respect him.'
verses.20:14: But when the vinedressers saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, 'This is the heir; let us slay him, that the inheritance may become ours.'
verses.20:15: So they cast him out of the vineyard and slew him. Therefore what will the master of the vineyard do to them?
verses.20:16: He will come and destroy these vinedressers, and give the vineyard to others." And when they heard it, they said, "May it never be!"
verses.20:17: Then He looked intently at them and said, "What then is this that is written: 'The stone which the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner'?
verses.20:18: Everyone who falls upon that stone will be shattered; but on whomever it falls, it will crush him to dust."
verses.20:19: And the scribes and the chief priests sought to lay hands upon Him in that very hour, yet they feared the people; for they knew that He had spoken this parable against them.
verses.20:20: And watching Him closely, they sent spies who pretended to be righteous men, that they might seize upon His words, so as to deliver Him up to the rule and authority of the governor.
verses.20:21: And they questioned Him, saying, "Teacher, we know that You speak and teach rightly, and show partiality to no one, but teach the way of God in truth:
verses.20:22: Is it lawful for us to pay tribute to Caesar, or not?"
verses.20:23: But perceiving their craftiness, He said to them,
verses.20:24: "Show Me a denarius. Whose image and inscription does it bear?" And they said, "Caesar's."
verses.20:25: And He said to them, "Therefore render the things of Caesar to Caesar, and the things of God to God."
verses.20:26: And they were not able to lay hold of His saying in the presence of the people; and marveling at His answer, they kept silent.
verses.20:27: Then certain of the Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, came up and questioned Him,
verses.20:28: saying, "Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man's brother dies, having a wife, and he is childless, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
verses.20:29: Now there were seven brothers; and the first took a wife and died childless;
verses.20:31: and the third took her; and in like manner the seven also left no children and died.
verses.20:33: Therefore in the resurrection, whose wife among them does she become? For the seven had her as wife."
verses.20:34: And Jesus said to them, "The sons of this age marry and are given in marriage;
verses.20:35: but those who are accounted worthy to attain to that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry nor are given in marriage;
verses.20:36: for neither are they able to die anymore, since they are equal to angels and are sons of God, being sons of the resurrection.
verses.20:37: Now that the dead are raised, even Moses showed at the bush, when he calls the Lord the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
verses.20:38: Yet He is not God of the dead, but of the living; for to Him all live."
verses.20:39: And certain of the scribes answered and said, "Teacher, You have spoken well."
verses.20:40: For they no longer dared to ask Him anything.
verses.20:41: Then He said to them, "How do they say that the Christ is the Son of David?
verses.20:42: For David himself says in the Book of Psalms, 'The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at My right hand,
verses.20:43: until I set Your enemies as a footstool for Your feet.'
verses.20:44: David therefore calls Him 'Lord,' and how is He his son?"
verses.20:45: Then, while all the people were listening, He said to His disciples,
verses.20:46: "Beware of the scribes, who desire to walk in long robes, and love greetings in the marketplaces, the chief seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets,
verses.20:47: who devour the houses of widows and for a pretense make long prayers. These shall receive a greater condemnation."
verses.21:1: Now looking up, He beheld the rich casting their gifts into the treasury.
verses.21:2: And He also saw a certain needy widow casting two small copper coins there,
verses.21:3: and He said, "Truly I say to you, this poor widow has cast in more than all of them;
verses.21:4: for all these out of their abundance have cast in among the gifts, yet she out of her poverty has cast in all the livelihood that she possessed."
verses.21:5: And as some were speaking concerning the temple, how it was adorned with fine stones and consecrated gifts, He said,
verses.21:6: "As for these things which you behold, days are coming in which stone shall not be left upon stone that shall not be torn down."
verses.21:7: And they questioned Him, saying, "Teacher, when then shall these things be, and what shall be the sign when these things are about to take place?"
verses.21:8: And He said, "Take heed that you are not led astray; for many shall come in My name, saying, 'I am he,' and, 'The time has drawn near.' Do not go after them.
verses.21:9: And when you hear of wars and tumults, do not be terrified; for these things must take place first, yet the end does not come immediately."
verses.21:10: Then He said to them, "Nation shall rise up against nation, and kingdom against kingdom;
verses.21:11: and there shall be great earthquakes, and in various places famines and pestilences; and there shall be dreadful terrors and great signs from heaven.
verses.21:12: Yet before all these things, they shall lay their hands upon you and persecute you, delivering you over to the synagogues and prisons, as you are brought before kings and governors for the sake of My name.
verses.21:13: It shall turn out for you as a testimony.
verses.21:14: Resolve therefore in your hearts not to rehearse beforehand how to make a defense,
verses.21:15: for I Myself will give you a mouth and wisdom which all those who oppose you shall not be able to withstand or contradict.
verses.21:16: Yet you shall be betrayed even by parents and brothers and kinsmen and friends, and they shall put some of you to death;
verses.21:17: and you shall be hated by all on account of My name.
verses.21:18: Yet not a single hair from your head shall ever perish.
verses.21:19: By your endurance, gain possession of your souls.
verses.21:20: Now when you see Jerusalem encircled by armies, then know that her desolation has drawn near.
verses.21:21: Then let those in Judea flee to the mountains, and let those in her midst depart, and let those in the countryside not enter her,
verses.21:22: because these are days of vengeance, so that all things which are written may be fulfilled.
verses.21:23: Yet woe to those who are with child and to those who are nursing in those days; for there shall be great distress upon the land and wrath against this people.
verses.21:24: And they shall fall by the edge of the sword and be taken captive into all the nations; and Jerusalem shall be trodden down by Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.
verses.21:25: And there shall be signs in the sun and moon and stars, and upon the earth anguish of nations in perplexity at the roaring of the sea and the surging waves,
verses.21:26: as men faint from terror and expectation of the things coming upon the inhabited world, for the powers of the heavens shall be shaken.
verses.21:27: And then they shall behold the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
verses.21:28: Now when these things begin to take place, stand upright and lift up your heads, because your redemption is drawing near."
verses.21:29: And He spoke a parable to them: "Behold the fig tree and all the trees.
verses.21:30: When they are already sprouting, seeing it, you know of yourselves that summer is already near.
verses.21:31: So you also, when you see these things taking place, know that the kingdom of God is near.
verses.21:32: Assuredly, I say to you that this generation shall by no means pass away until all things have come to pass.
verses.21:33: Heaven and earth shall pass away, yet My words shall never pass away.
verses.21:34: Now take heed to yourselves, lest your hearts be weighed down with dissipation and drunkenness and the anxieties of this life, and that day come upon you suddenly
verses.21:35: like a snare; for it shall come upon all those who dwell upon the face of all the earth.
verses.21:36: Yet stay awake at all times, praying that you may have strength to escape all these things that are about to take place, and to stand before the Son of Man."
verses.21:37: Now during the day He was teaching in the temple, yet at night He went out and lodged on the mount called Olivet.
verses.21:38: And all the people came early in the morning to Him in the temple to hear Him.
verses.22:1: Now the Feast of Unleavened Bread, which is called the Passover, was drawing near.
verses.22:2: And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking how they might slay Him, for they feared the people.
verses.22:3: Then Satan entered into Judas, who was called Iscariot, being one of the number of the twelve.
verses.22:4: And he departed and conferred with the chief priests and captains concerning how he might betray Him to them.
verses.22:5: And they rejoiced and agreed to give him silver.
verses.22:6: And he consented, and was seeking an opportunity to betray Him to them apart from a multitude.
verses.22:7: Then the Day of Unleavened Bread came, on which the Passover had to be sacrificed.
verses.22:8: And He sent forth Peter and John, saying, "Go and make ready the Passover for us, that we may eat."
verses.22:9: And they said to Him, "Where do You wish us to make ready?"
verses.22:10: And He said to them, "Behold, when you have entered into the city, a man bearing a jar of water will meet you; follow him into the house that he enters.
verses.22:11: And you shall say to the master of the house, 'The Teacher says to you, "Where is the guest chamber in which I may eat the Passover with My disciples?"'
verses.22:12: And he will show you a great upper room, furnished; make ready there."
verses.22:13: And departing, they found it just as He had told them, and they made ready the Passover.
verses.22:14: And when the hour had come, He reclined at the table, and the apostles with Him.
verses.22:15: And He said to them, "With earnest desire I have longed to eat this Passover with you before I suffer;
verses.22:16: for I say to you that I shall by no means eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God."
verses.22:17: And having received a cup, He gave thanks and said, "Take this and divide it among yourselves;
verses.22:18: for I say to you, from now on I shall by no means drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes."
verses.22:19: And taking bread, He gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, "This is My body, which is given on your behalf; do this in remembrance of Me."
verses.22:20: And in like manner the cup after supper, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out on your behalf.
verses.22:21: Yet behold, the hand of the one who betrays Me is with Me on the table.
verses.22:22: For indeed the Son of Man goes according to what has been determined, yet woe to that man by whom He is betrayed!"
verses.22:23: And they began to inquire among themselves which one of them it could be who was about to do this thing.
verses.22:24: Now a contention also arose among them as to which of them was regarded as the greatest.
verses.22:25: And He said to them, "The kings of the Gentiles rule as lords over them, and those who wield authority over them are called benefactors.
verses.22:26: Yet not so with you; instead, let the greatest among you become as the youngest, and the one who leads as the one who serves.
verses.22:27: For who is greater, the one who reclines at table or the one who serves? Is it not the one who reclines at table? Yet I am in your midst as the One who serves.
verses.22:28: Now you are those who have remained with Me in My trials;
verses.22:29: and I confer upon you, just as My Father conferred upon Me, a kingdom,
verses.22:30: so that you may eat and drink at My table in My kingdom, and sit upon thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
verses.22:31: Simon, Simon, behold, Satan has asked to have you, that he may sift you as wheat;
verses.22:32: but I have made supplication for you, that your faith may not fail; and you, when once you have turned back, strengthen your brethren."
verses.22:33: And he said to Him, "Lord, with You I am ready to go both to prison and to death."
verses.22:34: And He said, "I say to you, Peter, the rooster shall not crow this day until you have denied three times that you know Me."
verses.22:35: And He said to them, "When I sent you forth without a purse, or knapsack, or sandals, did you lack anything?" And they said, "Nothing."
verses.22:36: And He said to them, "But now, let the one who has a purse take it, and likewise a knapsack; and let the one who has none sell his cloak and buy a sword."
verses.22:37: "For I say to you that this which is written must be fulfilled in Me: 'And He was reckoned with the lawless'; for indeed what concerns Me has its fulfillment."
verses.22:38: And they said, "Lord, behold, there are two swords here." And He said to them, "It is enough."
verses.22:39: And going out, He proceeded according to custom to the Mount of Olives, and the disciples also followed Him.
verses.22:40: And when He arrived at the place, He said to them, "Pray that you do not enter into temptation."
verses.22:41: And He drew away from them about a stone's throw, and kneeling down, He prayed,
verses.22:42: saying, "Father, if You are willing, take away this cup from Me; yet let not My will, but Yours, be done."
verses.22:43: And an angel from heaven appeared to Him, strengthening Him.
verses.22:44: And being in agony, He prayed yet more fervently; and His sweat became like heavy drops of blood falling down upon the ground.
verses.22:45: And rising from prayer, He came to the disciples and found them asleep from sorrow,
verses.22:46: and said to them, "Why are you sleeping? Arise and pray, lest you enter into temptation."
verses.22:47: While He was still speaking, behold, a multitude came, and the one called Judas, one of the twelve, was going before them; and he approached Jesus to kiss Him.
verses.22:48: But Jesus said to him, "Judas, do you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?"
verses.22:49: And those around Him, seeing what was about to take place, said, "Lord, shall we strike with the sword?"
verses.22:50: And a certain one of them struck the servant of the high priest and severed his right ear.
verses.22:51: But Jesus answered and said, "No more of this." And touching his ear, He healed him.
verses.22:52: And Jesus said to the chief priests and captains of the temple and elders who had come against Him, "Have you come forth as against a robber, with swords and clubs?
verses.22:53: While I was with you daily in the temple, you did not stretch forth your hands against Me; yet this is your hour, and the authority of darkness."
verses.22:54: And having seized Him, they led Him away and brought Him into the house of the high priest; and Peter was following from afar.
verses.22:55: And when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the courtyard and seated themselves together, Peter sat in their midst.
verses.22:56: And a certain maidservant, seeing him sitting by the light and gazing intently at him, said, "This man also was with Him."
verses.22:57: But he denied it, saying, "I do not know Him, woman."
verses.22:58: And a short time later, another saw him and said, "You also are one of them." But Peter replied, "Man, I am not."
verses.22:59: And after an interval of about one hour, another firmly insisted, saying, "In truth this man also was with Him, for indeed he is a Galilean."
verses.22:60: And Peter said, "Man, I do not know what you are saying." And at once, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.
verses.22:61: And turning, the Lord looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how He had spoken to him, "Before a rooster crows this day, you shall deny Me three times."
verses.22:62: And going outside, he wept bitterly.
verses.22:63: Now the men who were holding Him were mocking Him and beating Him;
verses.22:64: and having blindfolded Him, they were questioning Him, saying, "Prophesy! Who is the one who struck You?"
verses.22:65: And blaspheming, they spoke many other things against Him.
verses.22:66: And when day broke, the assembly of the elders of the people came together—both chief priests and scribes—and they led Him away into their council,
verses.22:67: saying, "If You are the Christ, tell us." And He said to them, "If I tell you, you will certainly not believe;
verses.22:68: and if I question you, you will certainly not answer.
verses.22:69: Yet from this time onward the Son of Man shall be seated at the right hand of the power of God."
verses.22:70: And they all said, "Are You then the Son of God?" And He said to them, "You yourselves say that I am."
verses.22:71: And they said, "What further need do we have of testimony? For we ourselves have heard it from His mouth."
verses.23:1: Then the entire multitude of them rose up and brought Him before Pilate.
verses.23:2: And they began to accuse Him, saying, "We found this man subverting our nation, forbidding tribute to be paid to Caesar, and declaring that He Himself is Christ, a king."
verses.23:3: Then Pilate questioned Him, saying, "Are You the King of the Jews?" And answering him, He said, "You say so."
verses.23:4: Then Pilate said to the chief priests and the multitudes, "I find no guilt in this man."
verses.23:5: But they became all the more insistent, saying, "He stirs up the people, teaching throughout the whole of Judea, beginning even from Galilee to this place."
verses.23:6: When Pilate heard this, he inquired whether the man was a Galilean.
verses.23:7: And when he learned that He belonged to the jurisdiction of Herod, he sent Him away to Herod, who himself was also in Jerusalem during those days.
verses.23:8: Now when Herod saw Jesus, he rejoiced exceedingly, because for a long time he had desired to see Him on account of what he had heard concerning Him, and he was hoping to witness some sign performed by Him.
verses.23:9: And he questioned Him with many words, yet He made him no reply.
verses.23:10: Meanwhile, the chief priests and the scribes stood there, accusing Him vehemently.
verses.23:11: And Herod also, together with his soldiers, treated Him with contempt and mocked Him; and arraying Him in a splendid robe, he sent Him back to Pilate.
verses.23:12: And on that very day both Herod and Pilate became friends with one another, for previously they had been at enmity toward each other.
verses.23:13: Then Pilate summoned together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people,
verses.23:14: and said to them, "You have brought this man to me as one who turns the people astray; and behold, having examined Him in your presence, I have found no guilt in this man regarding any of the charges you bring against Him.
verses.23:15: No, nor did Herod, for he sent Him back to us; and behold, nothing deserving of death has been done by Him.
verses.23:16: Therefore, after chastising Him, I will release Him."
verses.23:18: But they cried out all together, saying, "Away with this man, and release Barabbas to us!"
verses.23:19: He was one who had been cast into prison on account of a certain insurrection that had taken place in the city, and for murder.
verses.23:20: Once more Pilate addressed them, desiring to release Jesus.
verses.23:21: But they kept shouting out, saying, "Crucify, crucify Him!"
verses.23:22: And a third time he spoke to them, "Why, what evil has this man committed? I have found no ground for death in Him; therefore, after chastising Him, I will release Him."
verses.23:23: Yet they pressed hard with loud voices, demanding that He be crucified; and their voices prevailed.
verses.23:24: So Pilate passed sentence that their demand should be granted.
verses.23:25: And he released the man who had been cast into prison for insurrection and murder, the one they had demanded; but Jesus he delivered up to their will.
verses.23:26: And as they led Him away, they seized a certain Simon of Cyrene who was coming in from the countryside, and placed the cross upon him to carry behind Jesus.
verses.23:27: Now a great multitude of the people was following Him, and women who were mourning and lamenting for Him.
verses.23:28: But turning toward them, Jesus said, "Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for Me; instead, weep for yourselves and for your children,
verses.23:29: for behold, days are coming in which they will say, 'Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that did not give birth, and the breasts that did not nurse.'
verses.23:30: Then they will begin to say to the mountains, 'Fall upon us!' and to the hills, 'Cover us!'
verses.23:31: For if they do these things with the green wood, what shall happen with the dry?"
verses.23:32: Now two others also, who were evildoers, were being led away with Him to be put to death.
verses.23:33: And when they arrived at the place called The Skull, there they crucified Him, along with the evildoers, one on the right and the other on the left.
verses.23:34: And Jesus kept saying, "Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing." And as they divided His garments, they cast lots.
verses.23:35: And the people stood watching; yet even the rulers scoffed, saying, "He saved others; let Him save Himself, if this man is the Christ of God, the Chosen One!"
verses.23:36: The soldiers likewise mocked Him, coming near and offering Him sour wine,
verses.23:37: and saying, "If You are the King of the Jews, save Yourself!"
verses.23:38: There was also an inscription above Him: "This is the King of the Jews."
verses.23:39: Then one of the evildoers who were hanged reviled Him, saying, "Are You not the Christ? Save Yourself and us!"
verses.23:40: But the other answered, rebuking him, and said, "Do you not even fear God, seeing that you are under the same judgment?
verses.23:41: And we indeed justly, for we are receiving what our deeds deserve; yet this man has done nothing amiss."
verses.23:42: And he said, "Jesus, remember me when You come in Your kingdom."
verses.23:43: And He said to him, "Assuredly, I say to you, this day you shall be with Me in Paradise."
verses.23:44: Now it was already about the sixth hour, and darkness fell over the whole land until the ninth hour,
verses.23:45: while the sun's light failed; and the veil of the temple was torn down the middle.
verses.23:46: And crying out with a loud voice, Jesus said, "Father, into Your hands I entrust My spirit." And when He had said this, He breathed His last.
verses.23:47: Now when the centurion saw what had taken place, he gave glory to God, saying, "Truly this man was righteous!"
verses.23:48: And all the multitudes who had gathered together for this spectacle, when they beheld the things that had taken place, turned back, beating their breasts.
verses.23:49: Yet all His acquaintances stood afar off, as well as the women who had accompanied Him from Galilee, looking upon these things.
verses.23:50: Now behold, there was a man named Joseph, who was a council member, a good and righteous man—
verses.23:51: he had not consented to their counsel and deed—from Arimathea, a city of the Jews, who was waiting for the kingdom of God;
verses.23:52: this man approached Pilate and requested the body of Jesus.
verses.23:53: And taking it down, he wrapped it in a linen shroud and laid Him in a tomb hewn from rock, in which no one had ever yet been laid.
verses.23:54: It was the day of Preparation, and the Sabbath was beginning to dawn.
verses.23:55: And the women who had come with Him from Galilee followed closely behind, and they beheld the tomb and how His body was laid.
verses.23:56: Then, returning home, they prepared spices and ointments. And throughout the Sabbath they rested in accordance with the commandment.
verses.24:1: Now on the first day of the week, at very early dawn, they came to the tomb, bringing the spices which they had prepared.
verses.24:2: And they found the stone rolled away from the tomb,
verses.24:3: but when they went inside, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
verses.24:4: And it came to pass, while they were perplexed over this, behold, two men stood beside them in dazzling apparel.
verses.24:5: And as they became terrified and bowed their faces to the ground, they said to them, "Why do you seek the Living One among the dead?
verses.24:6: He is not here, but has been raised! Remember how He spoke to you while He was still in Galilee,
verses.24:7: saying that the Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and on the third day rise again."
verses.24:9: and returning from the tomb, they reported all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.
verses.24:10: Now they were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, along with the other women who were with them; they told these things to the apostles.
verses.24:11: Yet these words appeared before them like idle talk, and they did not believe them.
verses.24:12: But Peter rose up and ran to the tomb; and stooping down, he beheld the linen cloths alone; and he departed to his own home, marveling at what had taken place.
verses.24:13: And behold, two of them were traveling that same day to a village sixty stadia distant from Jerusalem, named Emmaus,
verses.24:14: and they were conversing with one another about all these things that had happened.
verses.24:15: And it came to pass, while they were conversing and discussing together, that Jesus Himself drew near and journeyed with them,
verses.24:16: but their eyes were held fast, so that they did not recognize Him.
verses.24:17: And He said to them, "What are these words that you are exchanging with one another as you walk?" And they stood still, downcast in countenance.
verses.24:18: Then one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answered and said to Him, "Are You the only sojourner in Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in these days?"
verses.24:19: And He said to them, "What things?" And they said to Him, "The things concerning Jesus of Nazareth, who was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people,
verses.24:20: and how our chief priests and rulers delivered Him over to a sentence of death, and crucified Him.
verses.24:21: Yet we were hoping that He was the One about to redeem Israel. Indeed, besides all this, it is now the third day since these events took place.
verses.24:22: Moreover, certain women of our company astounded us, having been at the tomb early in the morning;
verses.24:23: and when they did not find His body, they came saying that they had also seen a vision of angels, who declared that He is alive.
verses.24:24: And certain of those who were with us went to the tomb, and found it just as the women had said; but Him they did not see."
verses.24:25: Then He said to them, "O foolish ones, and slow of heart to believe in all that the prophets have spoken!
verses.24:26: Was it not necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and to enter into His glory?"
verses.24:27: And beginning from Moses and from all the prophets, He interpreted to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself.
verses.24:28: And they drew near to the village where they were going, and He acted as though He would journey farther.
verses.24:29: But they strongly urged Him, saying, "Abide with us, for it is toward evening, and the day has already declined." And He went in to abide with them.
verses.24:30: And it came to pass, as He reclined with them, that taking the bread He blessed it, and having broken it, He gave it to them;
verses.24:31: and their eyes were opened, and they recognized Him; yet He vanished away from them.
verses.24:32: And they said to one another, "Was not our heart burning within us as He spoke to us on the road, as He opened the Scriptures to us?"
verses.24:33: And rising up that very hour, they returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven and those who were with them gathered together,
verses.24:34: saying, "Truly the Lord has been raised, and has appeared to Simon!"
verses.24:35: And they recounted what had occurred on the road, and how He was made known to them in the breaking of the bread.
verses.24:36: Now as they were speaking these things, He Himself stood in their midst and said to them, "Peace be to you."
verses.24:37: But startled and filled with fear, they supposed that they were beholding a spirit.
verses.24:38: And He said to them, "Why are you troubled, and why do doubts arise in your heart?
verses.24:39: Behold My hands and My feet, that it is I Myself. Touch Me and see, for a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you behold Me having."
verses.24:40: And having said this, He showed them His hands and His feet.
verses.24:41: Yet while they still disbelieved for joy and marveled, He said to them, "Do you have anything here to eat?"
verses.24:42: So they gave Him a piece of broiled fish;
verses.24:43: and taking it, He ate it before them.
verses.24:44: Then He said to them, "These are My words which I spoke to you while I was still with you, that everything written concerning Me in the Law of Moses and the Prophets and the Psalms must be fulfilled."
verses.24:45: Then He opened their mind to understand the Scriptures, and said to them,
verses.24:46: "Thus it is written, that the Christ should suffer and rise again from the dead on the third day,
verses.24:47: and that repentance for the remission of sins should be proclaimed in His name to all the nations—beginning from Jerusalem;
verses.24:48: you are witnesses of these things.
verses.24:49: And behold, I am sending the promise of My Father upon you; yet remain in the city until you are clothed with power from on high."
verses.24:50: And He led them out as far as Bethany, and lifting up His hands, He blessed them.
verses.24:51: And it came to pass, while He was blessing them, that He parted from them and was carried up into heaven.
verses.24:52: And they worshiped Him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
verses.24:53: and were continually in the temple, blessing God.

notes.1:22: The Greek adjective kophos rendered "speechless" can denote being mute, deaf, or both (compare 1:62, where signs are also made to Zechariah).
notes.1:28: The participle kecharitomene ("O favored one") literally means "one endowed with grace." Later manuscripts add "blessed are you among women" (likely assimilated from 1:42), which is absent from the earliest Greek witnesses followed here.
notes.1:35: The Greek clause may be construed either with "holy" as predicate ("the Child to be born shall be called holy, the Son of God") or as part of the subject ("that Holy One to be born shall be called the Son of God").
notes.1:37: Literally "no word from God shall be impossible" (or "void of power"), echoing Genesis 18:14 in the Septuagint; it may also be understood idiomatically as "nothing shall be impossible with God."
notes.1:45: The Greek conjunction hoti may be read either as introducing the content of Mary's faith ("believed that there shall be a fulfillment") or as causal ("believed, for there shall be a fulfillment").
notes.1:51: The past-tense (aorist) verbs in verses 51–54 reflect the biblical prophetic idiom of celebrating God's decisive saving works as already accomplished and certain.
notes.1:78: The Greek noun anatole ("Dawn" or "Dayspring") denotes the rising sun and also renders the Messianic title "Branch" in the Septuagint (e.g., Zechariah 3:8; 6:12). The earliest Greek manuscripts followed here read the future tense "shall visit," while later witnesses read "has visited."
notes.2:2: The Greek adjective rendered "first" can also be taken comparatively as "prior," indicating an enrollment made before Quirinius was governing Syria.
notes.2:14: The earliest Greek manuscripts read the genitive "of good pleasure" (referring to those upon whom God's favor rests), whereas later manuscripts read the nominative "goodwill."
notes.2:22: The critical Greek text reads the plural "their purification," referring to Mary and the Child (or the household), while some later manuscripts read "her purification."
notes.2:33: The earliest Greek manuscripts read "His father and His mother," whereas later manuscripts substitute "Joseph" for "His father."
notes.2:49: Literally "in the things of My Father," a Greek idiom that can mean either "in the house of My Father" or "about My Father's affairs."
notes.3:2: The Greek uses the singular title "high priest" for both Annas and Caiaphas; Annas had been deposed by Roman authorities yet retained enduring influence alongside his son-in-law Caiaphas, the officiating high priest.
notes.3:23: The Greek literally states that Jesus was "beginning, about thirty years [of age]," with "His ministry" understood from the context; the parenthetical "as was supposed" reflects the virgin conception.
notes.3:32: The Greek critical text reads "Jobel" (instead of Obed) and "Sala" (instead of Salmon), early manuscript readings preserved here rather than harmonized to the Old Testament forms.
notes.3:33: The Greek text includes both "Admin" and "Arni" between Amminadab and Hezron, corresponding to Ram/Aram in 1 Chronicles 2:9–10 and Matthew 1:3–4.
notes.3:36: The inclusion of "Cainan" between Shelah and Arphaxad follows the Septuagint genealogy of Genesis 11:12–13 rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.4:4: The earliest Greek manuscripts end the quotation of Deuteronomy 8:3 here without the longer clause "but by every word of God," which entered later manuscripts from Matthew 4:4.
notes.4:8: The critical Greek text omits "Get behind Me, Satan!" (added in later manuscripts in assimilation to Matthew 4:10) and opens Jesus' reply directly with "It is written."
notes.4:18: Luke quotes Isaiah 61:1-2 joined with Isaiah 58:6 from the Septuagint; the earliest manuscripts omit the phrase "to heal the brokenhearted" found in later textual traditions.
notes.4:44: The earliest Greek manuscripts read "Judea" rather than "Galilee," using "Judea" in Luke's broader sense for the entire Jewish homeland (compare Luke 1:5; 23:5).
notes.5:10: The Greek verb zogron literally means "catching alive," contrasting the apostles' new calling to bring people into life with their former work of catching fish.
notes.5:17: The Greek text reads "for Him to heal" (auton), referring to the Lord's power working through Jesus, rather than the later manuscript reading "to heal them."
notes.5:26: The Greek word paradoxa ("extraordinary things") occurs only here in the New Testament and denotes events contrary to or beyond human expectation.
notes.5:38: The Greek text concludes at "fresh wineskins," without the harmonized clause "and both are preserved" found in Matthew 9:17 and later manuscripts.
notes.5:39: The Greek text reads the positive adjective chrestos ("good") rather than the comparative reading "better" found in later manuscripts.
notes.6:1: Early critical manuscripts read simply "on a Sabbath"; later manuscripts add the obscure Greek term deuteroproto ("second-first"), whose meaning remains uncertain.
notes.6:16: The Greek literally reads "Judas of James"; while traditionally rendered "son of James," some understand the genitive to mean "brother of James."
notes.6:35: The Greek phrase meden apelpizontes can be understood either as "expecting nothing in return" or as "despairing of nothing" (while a manuscript variant medena yields "causing no one to despair").
notes.6:48: The critical Greek text reads "because it had been well built," whereas later manuscripts harmonize with Matthew 7:25 by reading "for it was founded upon the rock."
notes.7:11: The Greek phrase literally means "soon afterward" (in the time following); some manuscripts read the feminine dative, meaning "on the next day."
notes.7:19: The Greek text here reads "to Jesus," whereas some ancient manuscripts read "to the Lord."
notes.7:29: "Vindicated God" translates Greek edikaiosan ton theon (literally "justified God"), meaning they acknowledged God's righteousness; the same verb recurs in verse 35 ("wisdom is vindicated").
notes.7:47: Greek hoti ("for") may be taken evidentially ("as shown by the fact that she has loved much," harmonizing with the parable in verses 41-43) or causally; "for" retains the Greek structure.
notes.8:3: The Greek text reads "to them" (referring to Jesus and the twelve together), whereas some later manuscripts read "to Him."
notes.8:26: The Greek text reads "Gerasenes" (as also in 8:37), whereas other manuscripts read "Gadarenes" or "Gergesenes."
notes.8:44: The Greek word kraspedon refers to the border or tassel (fringe) worn on the corners of a Jewish outer garment in keeping with the Law (Numbers 15:38–39).
notes.8:51: The Greek text places John before James ("Peter and John and James"), following the earliest manuscript tradition.
notes.9:10: Many later manuscripts read "to a deserted place belonging to a city called Bethsaida," whereas the critical text reads simply "to a city called Bethsaida."
notes.9:24: The Greek word psyche can mean either "life" or "soul," holding both earthly existence and eternal life in view.
notes.9:29: The Greek participle rendered "dazzling" (exastrapton) literally means "flashing like lightning," depicting an intense, radiant brilliance.
notes.9:31: The Greek noun rendered "departure" is exodos ("exodus"), evoking Israel's deliverance and pointing to the redemptive fulfillment of Christ's death, resurrection, and ascension in Jerusalem.
notes.9:35: The critical text reads "the Chosen One" (eklelegmenos), echoing Isaiah 42:1, whereas many later manuscripts harmonize with Mark 9:7 and Matthew 17:5 by reading "the Beloved."
notes.9:51: The Greek noun rendered "being taken up" (analempsis) appears only here in the New Testament and looks ahead to Jesus' ascension as the culmination of His journey to Jerusalem.
notes.9:55: Some later manuscripts expand verses 54 through 56 with "just as Elijah did" and Jesus' rebuke, "You do not know what manner of spirit you are of; for the Son of Man did not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them," which are absent from the earliest witnesses.
notes.9:60: The saying "Leave the dead to bury their own dead" uses the first "dead" figuratively for those who remain spiritually outside the kingdom of God, underscoring the supreme urgency of proclaiming the gospel.
notes.10:1: The Greek critical text reads 'seventy-two' (hebdomekonta dyo, also in 10:17), whereas many later manuscripts read 'seventy.'
notes.10:15: The Greek question with me expects a negative answer; the critical text also reads the active/middle 'you shall descend' (katabese) rather than the passive 'you shall be brought down' found in later manuscripts.
notes.10:21: The Greek critical text specifies 'in the Holy Spirit' (to pneumati to hagio), whereas later manuscripts read simply 'in spirit.'
notes.10:42: The Greek critical text preserves the fuller reading 'yet few things are needed, or indeed one' (oligon de estin chreia e henos), which many manuscripts shorten to 'but one thing is needed.'
notes.11:2: The critical Greek text preserves Luke's shorter form of the Lord's Prayer, without the longer petitions harmonized from Matthew 6:9-13 in later manuscripts.
notes.11:3: The rare Greek adjective epiousios (rendered "daily") appears in the New Testament only in the Lord's Prayer and is variously understood as "daily," "for the coming day," or "necessary for subsistence."
